Any ideas? 那麼，我們計劃一下今天做什麼吧。有什麼主意？ Mr Chau Let's just go for a walk around the centre of London. 不如在倫敦市中心四處逛逛。 Angela Chau But Dad, the centre of London is really big. And it's too much walking. Let's do something else. 但爸爸，倫敦市中心很大，要走太多路了。做點其他事吧。 Mrs Chau Well, how about going to a museum? London has lots of excellent museums according to this website your Dad is looking at. Here are some exhibitions. 不如去博物館？爸爸正在看的網站說，倫敦有很多出色的博物館。這裡有一些展覽。 Angela Chau But museums are boring. Can't we do something more fun? 但博物館很悶。我們不能做些更有趣的事嗎？ Mr Chau Not all museums are boring. Have a look at this one. It's the Video Games Museum. 不是所有博物館都沉悶。看看這個，電子遊戲博物館。 Angela Chau Oh yes, that sounds interesting. What kind of video games do they have? 噢，聽起來有趣。它有什麼類型的電子遊戲？ Mrs Chau Let's have a look. 看看吧。 Mr Chau Oh, they have all kinds of video games, including a very early video game from 1958 called Tennis for Two. 它有各種電子遊戲，包括一款很早期、1958 年推出、叫 Tennis for Two 的遊戲。 Angela Chau Tennis for what? Tennis for 什麼？ Mr Chau Tennis for Two. Tennis for Two，即《雙人網球》。 Chau family Oh yes, and there's another one called Ping Pong from 1972. I remember that one. It's like table tennis. When is it from again? 還有另一款叫 Ping Pong，是 1972 年的。我記得它，像乒乓球。它是哪一年推出的？ Angela Chau That's so old! Are there any new games? 這麼古老！有新遊戲嗎？ Mrs Chau How about this one? 這個怎麼樣？ Mr Chau Teen Queen Four. Teen Queen Four，即《少女女王》第四集。 Angela Chau That's from this year, 2016. And all my friends have Teen Queen Four. 那是今年，即 2016 年推出的。我的朋友都有 Teen Queen Four。 Mr Chau Is there a Teen Queen Five? 有 Teen Queen Five 嗎？ Angela Chau No Dad, don't be silly. That's for next year. 沒有啦，爸爸，別傻了。那是明年的。 Mrs Chau Shall we go there then? Sounds good to me. 那我們去這裡吧？我覺得不錯。 Mr Chau Let's have a look at the opening times. Oh no, it's closed on Wednesdays so we can't go today. 看看開放時間。糟了，星期三休館，今天去不了。 Mrs Chau Oh. 噢。 Mr Chau Well, it's not the end of the world. We can go another day. Any other ideas? 又不是世界末日，可以改天再去。有其他主意嗎？ Mrs Chau What about this one? The Railway Museum. 這個呢？鐵路博物館。 Mr Chau The Railway Museum? 鐵路博物館？ Mrs Chau Yes. 對。 Angela Chau That sounds boring. 聽起來很悶。 Mrs Chau Maybe not. 未必吧。 Mr Chau It's in an old station and you get to ride on an old train. 它設於舊車站內，而且可以乘搭古老的火車。 Angela Chau Actually, that does sound boring. Boring. 其實那真的很悶。很悶。 Mr Chau No, it's not boring. And it's quite cheap too. It's only 250 Hong Kong dollars per person. 不，不悶，而且相當便宜，每人只需港幣二百五十元。 Angela Chau 250 dollars per person? That's expensive. 每人二百五十元？很貴。 Mrs Chau Yes, too expensive. 對，太貴了。 Angela Chau Plus it's boring. 而且很悶。 Mrs Chau Okay then. 那好吧。 Mr Chau I guess you're right. Let's look for something else. 我想你們說得對，再找別的吧。 Mrs Chau How about this one? 這個怎麼樣？ Angela Chau The Museum of Youth Culture. Youth Culture? That sounds all right. 青年文化博物館。青年文化？聽起來還不錯。 Mr Chau There's an exhibition about toy ponies. One of your favourite toys. 有一個關於玩具小馬的展覽，那是你最喜歡的玩具之一。 Mrs Chau You've still got your collection of toy ponies, haven't you? The My Pony Collection. 你還留着那套玩具小馬收藏吧？就是 My Pony Collection。 Angela Chau Yes, but I don't play with my ponies very much now. I'm a bit too old. 有，但我現在很少玩小馬了。我有點過了玩的年紀。 Mr Chau But you still like them. 但你仍然喜歡它們。 Angela Chau Yeah, I suppose so. 嗯，應該是吧。 Mr Chau Do you want to go see the exhibition of toy ponies? 你想去看玩具小馬展覽嗎？ Angela Chau Yes, okay. There's also an exhibition about boy bands. I don't like boy bands anymore. 好啊。這裡還有關於男子組合的展覽，但我已不再喜歡男子組合。 Mr Chau I thought you did. 我以為你喜歡。 Angela Chau Nope. 不喜歡了。 Mrs Chau How about this? 這個呢？ Angela Chau There's an exhibition on children's fashion. That sounds boring. 有一個兒童時裝展覽，聽起來很悶。 Mrs Chau No, but have a look at some of these pictures of the clothes. Don't they look interesting? 不，看看這些服裝圖片，不覺得很有趣嗎？ Angela Chau Oh yeah. Those clothes look pretty cool. I'd like to see that exhibition. 噢，對，那些衣服很酷。我想看這個展覽。 Mr Chau Finally, we've got a museum. Let's have a look at where the museum is. Oh no, it's quite far away. Let's have a look. 終於找到一間博物館了。看看它在哪裡。噢，距離挺遠。讓我看看。 Angela Chau Oh, but it's open late today. 不過今天開放到很晚。 Mr Chau Okay, so we can go there later. How much is it? 那可以遲些去。門票多少錢？ Mrs Chau Oh look, it's free for school children on Wednesdays. That means it's free for Angela today. 看，星期三學童免費，所以 Angela 今天不用付錢。 Mr Chau And one more thing. 還有一點。 Angela Chau What? 什麼？ Mr Chau It's interesting for all of us. 我們所有人都會覺得有趣。 Exam Narrator That is the end of task one. Okay, I suppose the most popular kind is a superhero comic. 女孩漫畫主要有兩類，第一類是幻想題材。哪類幻想？能舉例嗎？我想最受歡迎的就是超級英雄漫畫。 Chau family And what about the other kind? 另一類呢？ Angela Chau Well, the other main kind's real life. What did they have? 聽起來有趣，有什麼展品？ Chau family Well, one of the things they had was a Cabbage Patch doll. It was really popular in the 1980s. That doesn't sound very exciting. Well, actually millions of little girls. 這就是重點，人們正因為它醜才買它。難以置信，有多少小女孩會想要？事實上有數以百萬計。 Mr Chau Why were they so popular? 它為什麼這麼受歡迎？ Mrs Chau Well, I think it's because there were many different designs. 我想是因為有許多不同款式。 Mr Chau Many different designs? 許多不同款式？ Mrs Chau Yes, and this made them very collectible. 對，因此很有收藏價值。 Mr Chau So, ugly, but collectible dolls. Do you want one for your birthday, Angela? 所以是很醜、但值得收藏的娃娃。Angela，你想要它做生日禮物嗎？ Angela Chau Actually, I'd quite like one. I can look after it for a few years, so it increases in price. 其實我挺想要。我可以好好保存幾年，讓它升值。 Mr Chau That's my girl, always thinking ahead. What else did you see, Linda? 這才是我的女兒，總是想得長遠。Linda，你還看了什麼？ Mrs Chau Um, I saw one other thing that I think you would really like. 還有一樣，我想你會很喜歡。 Mr Chau Which is? 是什麼？ Mrs Chau A space hopper. 彈跳球。 Mr Chau A what? 什麼？ Mrs Chau A space hopper. It's like a big rubber ball. 彈跳球，就像一個大橡膠球。 Mr Chau A big rubber ball? 大橡膠球？ Mrs Chau Yes, and you sit on it and jump around. 對，你坐在上面四處跳。 Angela Chau Wow, jumping around. That sounds kind of fun. 嘩，跳來跳去，聽起來挺好玩。 Chau family But the best part was the extra things. You know the other things that kids used to do with space hoppers. Like what? Well, you can have a race. 最好玩的是其他玩法，就是以前小朋友會用彈跳球玩的其他遊戲。例如什麼？例如比賽競速。 Mr Chau Actually, me and my brother both had one. And as well as having races, it was really good fun having a fight. 其實我和弟弟以前各有一個。除了比賽，拿來打鬧也很好玩。 Mrs Chau You and your brother fighting. That doesn't surprise me. 你跟弟弟打鬧？一點也不意外。 Angela Chau Actually, this toy is beginning to sound awesome. Can we go back and see it, Mum? 這玩具聽起來愈來愈棒。媽媽，我們可以回去看看嗎？ Mrs Chau Sure, let's go. 當然，走吧。 Exam Narrator That is the end of task two. You now have one minute to tidy up your answer. 任務二完結。你現在有一分鐘整理答案。 青少年、漫畫與暢銷玩具 Chau 一家正在博物館內，談論剛看過的展品。請聆聽錄音，把缺漏資料填入以下空格。第一項已作為例子。 Chau 先生與 Angela 看過的展覽：「青少年與世界漫畫」（例子）。 女孩漫畫 國家： 。兩種主要漫畫類別： ，例如 ； ，例如 。 Angela 在香港購買的漫畫 購自 的商店。到那裡的原因： 。內容關於 ，例如 。 Chau 太太看過的展覽：「昔日暢銷玩具」 展品一：Cabbage Patch Doll（椰菜娃娃）圖片。 流行於 。受歡迎的原因： ； 。 展品二：Space Hopper（彈跳球）圖片。 它是什麼： 。基本玩法： 。另外兩種彈跳球玩法： ； 。

entries.title: Young Inventors
entries.text: The Chau family are looking at an exhibition in the museum called Young Inventors. A guide is showing them around this exhibition. Listen and fill in the missing information in the spaces below. The first one has been provided as an example. Invention 1: Shoe battery charger Name of inventor: Juan Domingo Origin of the idea The inventor walks 5 km to school every day (example) . He realized that this is The average person takes How the invention works Step on the Footsteps generate This is converted to electricity. Electricity is stored in batteries, which are attached to Examples of use Ninety minutes of = fifteen minutes of electricity for Another application of the shoes: Who thinks the invention is useful? (You can tick one or more options.) Angela Mr Chau Mrs Chau Invention 2: Smelly Alarm Clock Name of inventor: Jean-Paul Moncoeur Origin of the idea His father the sound of an alarm clock and so Further details Smell that works best is The device towards the person who is sleeping. Most people wake up and Who likes the invention? (You can tick one or more options.) Angela Mr Chau Mrs Chau Exam Narrator Task three. The Chau family are looking at an exhibition in the museum called Young Inventors. A guide is showing them around this exhibition. Listen and fill in the missing information in the spaces below. The first one has been provided as an example. You now have 30 seconds to study the task. 任務三。Chau 一家正在博物館參觀名為「年輕發明家」的展覽，由導賞員帶領。請聆聽錄音，把缺漏資料填入以下空格。第一項已作為例子。你現在有三十秒閱讀題目。 Exam Narrator At the end of the task, you will have one and a half minutes to tidy up your answers. 任務結束後，你將有一分半鐘整理答案。 Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas) Hello, everyone. My name is Sakari Douglas and I'll be your guide for this section of the museum. Today, I'll be showing you the exhibition on Young Inventors and I hope you enjoy the tour. 大家好，我叫 Sakari Douglas，是博物館這個展區的導賞員。今天會帶大家參觀「年輕發明家」展覽，希望各位享受導賞。 Mrs Chau It sounds really interesting. Do you think it will inspire you to try some inventions of your own, Angela? 聽起來很有趣。Angela，你覺得這會啟發你嘗試自己的發明嗎？ Angela Chau Not likely. I'm no good at science. 不大可能，我不擅長科學。 Mr Chau But I don't think all the inventions are about science. Let's have a look at them. 但我想不是所有發明都與科學有關，先看看吧。 Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas) So, our first exhibit is the Shoe Battery Charger. This was invented by Juan Domingo from the Philippines and he was only 14 when he invented it. The inventor walks five kilometers to school every day. I know this seems a lot, but in the countryside in the Philippines, many school children have to do the same. Anyway, the inventor thought that this is a lot of wasted energy. 第一件展品是鞋子電池充電器，由菲律賓的 Juan Domingo 發明，當時他只有十四歲。他每天步行五公里上學。我知道看來很遠，但在菲律賓鄉郊，很多學童都一樣。他想到，這其實浪費了很多能量。 Mr Chau Wow. A five kilometer walk to school every day? That's pretty far. Would you like to walk that far to school, Angela? 嘩，每天走五公里上學？挺遠的。Angela，你願意走那麼遠上學嗎？ Angela Chau Not likely. I'm not going to waste all that energy. 不可能，我才不會浪費那麼多能量。 Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas) Well, actually, according to the inventor, on average, people take 7,000 footsteps a day. 其實，根據發明者所說，人們平均每天走七千步。 Mrs Chau That seems a lot. So how does the shoe work? 似乎很多。那鞋子怎樣運作？ Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas) Well, there are different stages to the process and let me show you. Here is the shoe and inside each shoe are two electrical discs. First, the person wearing the shoe steps on the electrical discs every time they take a footstep. Second, each footstep generates pressure on the disc. And third, this pressure is then converted to electricity. 過程分幾個階段，我示範一下。這是鞋子，每隻鞋內有兩塊電力圓片。第一，穿鞋者每走一步都會踩到圓片。第二，每步會對圓片產生壓力。第三，壓力轉化為電力。 Mrs Chau So how do you store the electricity? 那怎樣儲存電力？ Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas) You need a battery and you attach it to the outside of your shoes. 需要一顆電池，把它裝在鞋子外面。 Angela Chau／Museum Guide I've got a question. Yes. How much electricity do the shoes generate? 我有問題。請說。鞋子能產生多少電力？ Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas) That's a good question, actually. At the moment, not so much. But this is the first model. The inventor gave an example of when he played basketball for an hour and a half. He managed to generate 15 minutes of battery power for a mobile phone. 好問題。現時不太多，但這只是第一個型號。發明者舉例說，他打了一個半小時籃球，產生的電池電量足夠手機使用十五分鐘。 Angela Chau That's not very much. 不算很多。 Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas) That's right. But there is one other application that the inventor has suggested. This electricity can be used to power a light and this doesn't need so much power. Any other questions? 對，不過發明者另提了一種用途：電力可以用來照明，而燈所需的電量較少。還有問題嗎？ Mrs Chau What do you think, Angela? Angela，你覺得怎樣？ Angela Chau Well, I wouldn't like to do all the walking, but it certainly is useful. 我不想走那麼多路，但它肯定有用。 Mrs Chau What do you think, Dad? 爸爸，你覺得呢？ Mr Chau I think it's great. 我覺得很棒。 Mrs Chau I worry that it's not practical, and you won't be able to produce enough electricity. Surely, traditional batteries are better. 我擔心它不實用，產生不了足夠電力。傳統電池應該更好吧。 Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas) Okay, let's move on to our next invention. Just over here. Can everybody see? 我們看下一項發明，就在這裡。大家看得到嗎？ Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas) This invention is the smelly alarm clock. The inventor of this is Jean-Paul Moncoeur, and he's from Canada. This 17-year-old invented the device for his father, who is deaf, or hard of hearing, I should say. Jean-Paul invented this to help his father, who couldn't hear the sound of an alarm clock. As a result of this, very often his father was late for work and almost lost his job. 這是氣味鬧鐘，發明者是加拿大的 Jean-Paul Moncoeur。這位十七歲少年為父親發明了它；父親失聰，或更準確地說是聽力不佳，聽不到鬧鐘聲，因此經常上班遲到，幾乎失去工作。 Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas) Jean-Paul had the brilliant idea of using the sense of smell instead of sound to wake people up. Jean-Paul 想到一個妙計：用嗅覺代替聲音，喚醒睡覺的人。 Mrs Chau Sorry to interrupt, but what smell did Jean-Paul find was the most effective to wake people up? 抱歉打斷一下，Jean-Paul 發現哪種氣味最能喚醒人？ Chau family／Museum Guide That's a good question, and the answer is peppermint. Peppermint? Yes, peppermint. 好問題，答案是薄荷。薄荷？對，薄荷。 Mr Chau So, how does the device work then? 這裝置怎樣運作？ Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas) Well, first you place some peppermint tablets inside the alarm clock, and then you set the alarm. When the alarm goes off, a fan blows air towards the sleeper. 首先把薄荷片放入鬧鐘，再設定鬧鐘時間。鬧鐘啟動時，風扇會向睡着的人吹氣。 Angela Chau But does it really work? 但真的有效嗎？ Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas) Oh yes, and you know that most people hate getting up early in the morning. Well, the inventor reckons that most people wake up in a good mood. 有，而且你知道大部分人都討厭清早起床。發明者認為，大部分人醒來時心情愉快。 Mrs Chau Really, that sounds good to me. 真的？聽起來不錯。 Mr Chau Mmm, sounds too good to be true to me. 嗯，對我來說聽起來好得令人難以置信。 Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas) And one more thing, apparently you also wake up feeling refreshed. 還有一點，據說醒來後也會感到精神煥發。 Mr Chau No, I'm not convinced. 不，我還未被說服。 Mrs Chau I am? I think it sounds fantastic. What do you think, Angela? 我就信了。我覺得很棒。Angela，你怎麼看？ Angela Chau I think I agree with Dad on this one. 這次我想我同意爸爸。 Exam Narrator That is the end of task three. You now have one and a half minutes to tidy up your answers. 任務三完結。你現在有一分半鐘整理答案。 年輕發明家 Chau 一家正在博物館參觀名為「年輕發明家」的展覽，由導賞員帶領。請聆聽錄音，把缺漏資料填入以下空格。第一項已作為例子。 發明一：鞋子電池充電器 發明者姓名：Juan Domingo。 構思來源 發明者每天步行五公里上學（例子）。他發覺這是 。一般人平均會走 。 發明的運作原理 步驟一：踏在 上。步驟二：腳步產生 。步驟三：這轉化為電力。步驟四：電力儲存在電池內，電池裝在 。 用途例子 九十分鐘＝足供 使用十五分鐘的電力。鞋子的另一用途： 。 第 40 題：誰認為這項發明有用？（可選一項或以上。）A Angela；B Chau 先生；C Chau 太太。 發明二：氣味鬧鐘 發明者姓名：Jean-Paul Moncoeur。 構思來源 他的父親 鬧鐘聲，所以 。 其他詳情 最有效的氣味是 。裝置會朝着熟睡的人 。大部分人醒來時 ，而且 。 第 47 題：誰喜歡這項發明？（可選一項或以上。）A Angela；B Chau 先生；C Chau 太太。

entries.title: James Dean and Rebel Without a Cause
entries.text: The Chau family are attending a lecture given by David Stott about movie stars that are popular with young people. Listen to the lecture and answer the questions below. You do not need to answer in complete sentences. The first one has been provided as an example. James Dean James Dean If people have not seen a James Dean movie, in what three ways might people recognize him? From a work of art (example) Give two reasons why he is still so famous. Why was he fired from his job as a stunt tester? What was special about the movie Rebel Without a Cause ? Before Rebel Without a Cause , what kind of roles did young people have in movies? What was the purpose of having young people in movies before Rebel Without a Cause ? What three effects did Rebel Without a Cause have on the movie industry? Exam Narrator Task four. The Chau family are attending a lecture given by David Stott about movie stars that are popular with young people. 任務四。Chau 一家正在聽 David Stott 的講座，主題是受年輕人歡迎的電影明星。 Exam Narrator Listen to the lecture and answer the questions below. Please note, you do not need to answer in complete sentences. 請聆聽講座，回答下列問題。注意：不必用完整句子作答。 Exam Narrator The first one has been provided as an example. 第一項已作為例子。 Exam Narrator You now have 30 seconds to study the task. 你現在有三十秒閱讀題目。 Exam Narrator At the end of the task, you will have two minutes to tidy up your answers. 任務結束後，你將有兩分鐘整理答案。 David Stott Hello everyone. My name is David Stott and I'm here to talk to you about one American movie star from the 1950s who has perhaps had the biggest influence on young people all over the world. So, who is this movie star? Well, of course, it's James Dean. Even if you don't know his name or have never seen him in a movie, you still might recognize him. How? Well, you might see his image in a work of art such as a painting or a screen print. 大家好，我叫 David Stott。今天要談一位二十世紀五十年代的美國影星，他可能是對全球年輕人影響最大的影星。他是誰？當然是 James Dean。即使不知道他的名字、從未看過他的電影，你仍可能認得他。怎樣認得？你可能在油畫或絲網版畫等藝術作品中見過他的形象。 David Stott He has featured in some of the most famous art of the last century. Apart from art, you might see a photo of him on someone's wall or in a restaurant. Obviously a black and white photo as it would have been taken in the 1950s. Or you might hear his name in the lyrics to a pop song, which would be something about looking like James Dean or smoking like James Dean, driving a fast car like James Dean, or just being cool like James Dean. 上世紀一些最著名藝術作品都有他。除了藝術，你可能在別人家中牆上或餐廳看過他的照片；當然是黑白照，因為拍於五十年代。又或者，你可能在流行曲歌詞中聽到他的名字，內容是像 James Dean 一樣的外貌、像他那樣抽煙、開快車，或者只是像他那麼酷。 David Stott He is one of the most recognizable people of the last century. But why is he so recognizable? I mean, why is James Dean still so famous even today? Well, one of the things that ensured he would be a legend is that he died so young. He died at the age of 24, and so his good looks never faded. The other reason why his fame continues today is that he died tragically in a car crash. 他是上世紀最容易被認出的人之一。但為何如此？為什麼直到今天仍這麼有名？一個令他成為傳奇的原因，是他英年早逝：二十四歲就離世，因此俊朗外貌從未衰退。另一個讓他至今有名的原因，是他在車禍中悲劇性地喪生。 David Stott This, I think, contributes significantly to his continuing fame. What's even more surprising is that James Dean wasn't one of those actors who made a lot of films. His fame rests on his roles in just three movies, and I'm going to talk about those in a moment. Actually, fame did not arrive so easily for James Dean. Before he made these three movies, he was involved in acting, 我認為這對他持續的名氣影響很大。更令人意外的是，他並不是拍了很多電影的演員。他的名氣建基於三部電影的角色，我稍後會談。其實他並非輕易成名；拍這三部電影之前，他已有演戲， David Stott but only had small roles and he had to supplement his income with other jobs, such as a stunt tester on a TV game show called Beat the Clock. And he was actually fired. Why? It's quite ironic, really. In this TV show, contestants had to do stunts inside a certain time limit. One of the typical stunts was like, say, contestants had to pick up and carry an egg across a room in 30 seconds, 但只有小角色，要靠其他工作補貼收入，例如在電視遊戲節目 Beat the Clock 做特技測試員。他還被解僱了。為什麼？很諷刺。節目參賽者須在時限內完成特技，例如在三十秒內拿起一隻雞蛋並帶到房間另一邊， David Stott but they weren't allowed to use their hands. That sort of thing. James Dean's job was as a stunt tester, so he had to test the stunts to see whether they would be possible to do inside the time limit. Actually, he was so good at doing the stunts and so quick that he was fired from the show. 但不准用手，就是這類項目。James Dean 的工作是測試特技是否能在時限內完成。可是他做得太好、太快，反而被節目解僱。 David Stott As I said earlier, his fame rests on just three movies, East of Eden, Rebel Without a Cause, and Giant. It is the second of these movies, Rebel Without a Cause, filmed in 1955, that has been the most influential in popular culture. So what's so special about Rebel Without a Cause? 正如之前所說，他的名氣建基於三部電影：《天倫夢覺》、《阿飛正傳》和《巨人傳》。其中第二部、1955 年拍攝的《阿飛正傳》，對流行文化最有影響。它究竟有什麼特別？ David Stott Well, for the first time ever in the movies, Rebel Without a Cause showed the problems faced by a typical teenager in the 1950s. So what were these problems that teenagers faced back then? Well, they were pretty similar to those teenagers faced nowadays. But as I say, what made it special was that these problems had never been shown in movies before. 它是電影史上第一次呈現五十年代一般青少年面對的問題。當時青少年遇到什麼問題？其實與現今青少年很相似。但正如我所說，特別之處在於這些問題以前從未在電影中出現。 David Stott Before that time, and I know this sounds crazy now, middle-aged adults usually had the leading roles. Young people played roles such as sons and daughters of the main characters. So why were young people even in movies? Well, young people were usually just there to show that the main characters, the adult characters, were happily married and had a happy family. 在此之前——我知道現在聽來很不可思議——主角通常是中年人，年輕人只扮演主角的兒女。那為何電影還要有年輕人？通常只是用來顯示成年主角婚姻美滿、家庭幸福。 David Stott So typically, young people were on the screen for only five to ten minutes in the entire film. And that was it. 因此，年輕人在整部電影裡通常只出現五至十分鐘，僅此而已。 David Stott James Dean and his role in Rebel Without a Cause changed all of that. It was as though Hollywood and the US movie-going public suddenly woke up. This had three huge effects on the movie industry. Firstly, a large number of movies about teenagers began to be made. Before this, as I said earlier, movies were always about adults. James Dean 在《阿飛正傳》中的角色改變了一切，彷彿荷里活與美國觀眾突然醒覺。這為電影業帶來三大影響。第一，開始大量製作關於青少年的電影；此前電影總是以成人為主題。 David Stott The second major effect was that this kind of film began to be made in many different countries, so it wasn't just in Hollywood. It was in movie industries all over the world that films about teenagers started to be produced. And thirdly, and perhaps most importantly, young people, who had been ignored by the movie industry, were targeted as an audience by the movie industry. So young people became the target audience. 第二，許多不同國家開始製作這類電影，不再只是荷里活，而是世界各地電影業都開始拍青少年題材。第三，或許最重要的是，以前被忽略的年輕人，成為電影業針對的觀眾群，即目標觀眾。 David Stott OK, let's fast forward 40 years to the rise of another movie star, Johnny Depp. 好的，現在快進四十年，談另一位影星 Johnny Depp 的崛起。 Exam Narrator That is the end of task four. It was fine all week. And then suddenly, at the weekend, it became really, 我不知道。牠整個星期都好好的，到了週末卻突然病得非常、 Editorial meeting really sick. Oh, that's terrible. Well, I hope your dog gets better soon. 非常嚴重。真糟糕。希望你的狗快點康復。 Editorial meeting Thanks. How about you? How was yours? Well, I don't mean to gloat, but I had a great weekend. 謝謝。你呢？你的週末怎樣？我不是想炫耀，不過我過了個很棒的週末。 Editorial meeting A really wonderful weekend. Do you want to know why? Let me tell you. I bought a new TV, 真的非常愉快。想知道原因嗎？讓我告訴你：我買了部新電視， Editorial meeting one of those really, really big TVs. It's totally amazing. It's like real life. 就是那種非常、非常大的電視，實在太棒了，畫面就像真實世界一樣。 Editorial meeting Wow. That sounds cool. I would love to have a big TV like that. Oh, here comes Katie 嘩，聽起來很不錯。我也想有一部那樣的大電視。噢，Kaity 現在 Editorial meeting now. Morning, guys. Sorry, I'm a bit late. Morning, Katie. 來了。各位早安，對不起，我遲了一點。早安，Kaity。 Editorial meeting So, how was your weekend, Katie? Boring, boring, boring. Kaity，你的週末怎樣？無聊、無聊、無聊。 Editorial meeting Why, why, why? Because I had to work, work, work, Dan. That's my reward for being the 為什麼、為什麼、為什麼？因為我得工作、工作、工作，Dan。這大概就是當 Editorial meeting boss, I suppose, having to work all weekend. Oh, well. 老闆的「回報」吧：整個週末都要工作。唉。 Editorial meeting Right now, we've got lots to get through. So, for the June edition of the magazine, 好了，現在有很多事情要處理。六月號雜誌的 Editorial meeting our main theme will be games and play. Now, I sent out an email last week asking us all to 主要主題是遊戲和玩樂。我上星期發了電郵，請大家 Editorial meeting come up with ideas for topics. Dan? Well, I was thinking of computer games and learning, 想一些題材。Dan？我想到電腦遊戲與學習， Editorial meeting you know, like games that actually teach you a skill. There's one called The Next Mozart. 就是那些真的能教你一項技能的遊戲。有一款叫《下一個莫扎特》。 Editorial meeting It's like a piano playing game. My niece is always playing it. 那是類似彈鋼琴的遊戲，我的姪女經常玩。 Editorial meeting Yeah, that is a good topic. I'll definitely accept it for the next edition. These computer 對，這個題材很好，下一期一定採用。這類用來 Editorial meeting games for learning are really popular. Right, and what have you got for us, Iris? 學習的電腦遊戲很受歡迎。那 Iris，你有什麼建議？ Editorial meeting Well, I've been looking at games that young children play in the playground. 我在研究小朋友在遊樂場玩的遊戲。 Editorial meeting Do you mean like playground games? Yeah, that's right. Playground games. 你是指遊樂場遊戲嗎？對，就是遊樂場遊戲。 Editorial meeting I was thinking of looking at some examples, you know, like Catch the Dragon and, um, 我想介紹一些例子，例如《捉龍》，還有，嗯， Editorial meeting Fingers Out. Oh, yeah. Did you say Fingers Out? I remember Fingers Out. I used to play that 《伸出手指》。噢，你剛才說《伸出手指》嗎？我記得，我以前 Editorial meeting all the time when I was at primary school. What was the first game called again? Um, 讀小學時經常玩。第一款遊戲叫什麼？嗯， Editorial meeting The Dragon One. Catch the Dragon. Oh, right. Not sure if I ever played that one. 那個跟龍有關的。《捉龍》。噢，我不肯定自己有沒有玩過。 Editorial meeting Oh, I did. Definitely. Anyway, this is a great topic, Iris. 我有，肯定有。總之，Iris，這題材很好。 Editorial meeting So you accept it? Yep, definitely. Playground games are fun to watch. 那你採用嗎？對，一定採用。遊樂場遊戲看起來很有趣。 Editorial meeting Lots and lots of fun to watch. So right back to you, Dan. Uh, any other contributions? 看起來真的非常有趣。好，再回到 Dan，你還有其他建議嗎？ Editorial meeting Yes. So something I've been looking at is computer games for animals. 有。我最近在研究供動物玩的電腦遊戲。 Editorial meeting I think it would be nice to contrast human games with like games animals play. 我覺得把人類玩的遊戲和動物玩的遊戲作比較會很不錯。 Editorial meeting Well, it sounds interesting. What do you mean by computer games for animals exactly? 聽起來很有意思。你說的動物電腦遊戲究竟是什麼？ Editorial meeting Well, there’s loads of videos on the internet. Dogs and cats jumping at moving objects on the 網上有很多影片，狗和貓朝着 Editorial meeting computer screen. It's really funny. There's this one game you can get for computer tablets called 電腦螢幕上移動的物件跳來跳去，非常搞笑。有一款平板電腦遊戲叫 Editorial meeting Crazy Cat. It's brilliant. The cat chases a red dot around the screen. 《瘋狂貓咪》。很好玩的，貓會追着螢幕上的紅點跑。 Editorial meeting Dan, you're not getting paid to look at funny videos on the internet. Dan，我付薪水給你，不是讓你在網上看搞笑影片。 Editorial meeting What research have you done? Really? Crazy Cat? Um, no research. Sorry. 你做過什麼研究？真的嗎，《瘋狂貓咪》？嗯，沒有研究，對不起。 Editorial meeting Will you accept my topic though? Dan, you haven't done any research, 不過你會採用我的題材嗎？Dan，你沒有做任何研究， Editorial meeting so it's a no. I can't accept topics that haven't been researched. 所以不會。我不能採用未經研究的題材。 Editorial meeting / Narrator Yeah, okay. That is the end of task one. 好吧。任務一完結。 Narrator You now have one minute to tidy up your answers. 你現在有一分鐘整理答案。 下一期雜誌 Kaity Chandra 是雜誌編輯。她正與兩位記者 Iris Mu 和 Dan Lai 開會，討論下一期雜誌。請聆聽討論，並在下面空格填寫缺漏資料。其中一項已作為例子提供。 Iris、Dan 和 Kaity 週末做了什麼？ 表格欄目：人物／週末／原因。 Iris：她度過了一個 的週末，因為她的 。 Dan：他度過了一個 的週末，因為他 。 Kaity：她度過了一個 的週末，因為她 。 下一期雜誌的建議題材。 表格欄目：題材（遊戲與玩樂）／遊戲名稱／Kaity 是否採用？／原因。 用來學習的電腦遊戲：《下一個莫扎特》（The Next Mozart）；是；這些遊戲很受歡迎（例子）。 ： 、 ；是； 。 ： ；否； 。

entries.title: Monster Maze
entries.text: Iris is working on an online game for the next issue of the magazine. There are three parts to Task 2. In Part A, Iris explains the game to Dan. In Part B, Dan plays the game. In Part C, Dan and Iris discuss the game. Part A — Monster Maze key Fill in the missing information in the spaces provided in the Monster Maze key. E4 D1 C5 B2 O O O O O O M Directions: ↑ Forward · ← Left · → Right · ↓ Backward = O = route taken M = landed on a hidden monster Part B Plot Dan’s route by putting a circle (O) in each square like the example shown above in the Monster Maze key and put an M if he lands on a hidden monster. Dan’s first life E6 D1 B2 Dan’s second life E1 E6 D1 B2 Part C Listen to Iris and Dan’s discussion and answer the questions. You do not have to answer in full sentences. What are Dan’s suggestions for improving the Monster Maze game? How will people play the game online? How can the player trust that the game doesn’t cheat when placing the monsters? First, when the game starts, Second, when the game’s over, Third, Fourth, Narrator Task two. Iris is working on an online game for the next issue of the magazine. 任務二。Iris 正在為下一期雜誌製作一個網上遊戲。 Narrator There are three parts to task two. In part A, Iris explains the game to Dan. 任務二分為三部分。甲部分，Iris 向 Dan 解釋遊戲。 Narrator In part B, Dan plays the game. In part C, Dan and Iris discuss the game. 乙部分，Dan 玩遊戲。丙部分，Dan 和 Iris 討論遊戲。 Narrator You now have 30 seconds to study the task. At the end of the task, 你現在有三十秒閱讀題目。本任務結束後， Narrator you will have one minute to tidy up your answers. Part A. Fill in the missing information 你將有一分鐘整理答案。甲部分：請填上缺漏資料， Narrator in the spaces provided in the monster maze key. 寫在「怪物迷宮」圖例所提供的空格內。 Iris and Dan Hey Iris, what are you working on? Well, for this edition of the magazine, Iris，你在做什麼？我正在為這一期雜誌 Iris and Dan I'm designing some games. You know, so that our subscribers can play them on their phone. 設計一些遊戲，讓訂戶可以用手機玩。 Iris and Dan The idea is that they pay money to play and they can win money if they win. 構思是他們付費玩遊戲，如果勝出便可以贏錢。 Iris and Dan Cool. What kind of games? Well, the one I'm working on just now is called monster maze. 很棒。是什麼遊戲？我現在做的這個叫「怪物迷宮」。 Iris and Dan Have a look. That's the key. I'm just finishing the example for the key just now. 看看吧，這是圖例。我剛好在完成圖例中的示範。 Iris and Dan Hmm. The grid looks good. 嗯，格子看起來不錯。 Iris and Dan Okay, good. So where's the entrance to the maze? Is it at the top here? 好。迷宮入口在哪裡？在上面這裡嗎？ Iris and Dan No, the other way round. The entrance to the maze is at the bottom where the numbers 1 to 6 are. 不，剛好相反。入口在下面，有一至六這些數字的地方。 Iris and Dan Ah, I see. Where the numbers are. So the exit to the maze is at the top then? 明白，在數字那邊。那麼出口在上面嗎？ Iris and Dan Exactly. The exit's at the top. 沒錯，出口在上面。 Iris and Dan Oh, okay. Right. And the grey squares must be walls or something. 好。那些灰色格子應該是牆壁之類的東西吧。 Iris and Dan Yes, that's right. The grey squares are the walls of the maze. 對，灰色格子就是迷宮的牆壁。 Iris and Dan And those circles, the O's, that indicates the route you've taken through the maze. 那些圓圈，也就是 O，代表你走過迷宮的路線。 Iris and Dan Oh, I see the O's. And what's this M here? 我看到 O 了。那這個 M 是什麼？ Iris and Dan That's the monster. There are three, but they're hidden when you play the game. 那是怪物。共有三隻，不過玩遊戲時牠們是隱藏的。 Iris and Dan But when you land on one of the monsters, an M appears and you lose a life. 當你走到其中一隻怪物所在的格子，便會出現 M，而你會失去一條生命。 Iris and Dan Right. Still not sure if I get it. 好，我還是不太肯定自己是否明白。 Iris and Dan So have a look at the example in the key. 看看圖例中的例子吧。 Iris and Dan Okay. Well, in the example, the player starts on A4, goes forward one square to B4, 好。例子中的玩家由 A4 開始，向前走一格到 B4， Iris and Dan moves left one square to B3, moves forward three squares to E3, and then moves left one square. 再向左一格到 B3，向前走三格到 E3，然後向左一格。 Iris and Dan And there at E2, he lands on the monster. 於是在 E2，他遇上怪物。 Iris and Dan And is dead. 然後就死了。 Iris and Dan Yep. 對。 Iris and Dan Eaten alive. 被活生生吃掉了。 Iris and Dan Exactly. 沒錯。 Narrator Part B. Plot Dan's route by putting a circle in each square like the example shown above 乙部分：請像上面圖例中的示範一樣，在每一格畫圓圈，標示 Dan 的路線， Narrator in the monster maze key, and put an M if he lands on a hidden monster. 並在他遇上隱藏怪物的格子填上 M。 Iris and Dan So, do you want to play, Dan? Dan，你想玩嗎？ Iris and Dan Sure. 當然。 Iris and Dan Okay. We can do it without the computer just now. So, I'll hide three monsters on the grid 好，現在不用電腦也能玩。我先把三隻怪物藏在格子裡， Iris and Dan by writing down the grid number, and you have to go from the entrance of the maze 把格子座標寫下來，你要由迷宮入口 Iris and Dan and reach the exit without walking into the monsters. You get two lives. 走到出口，不能碰上怪物。你有兩條生命。 Iris and Dan Sure. So, this is my first life, eh? 好，這是我的第一條生命，對吧？ Iris and Dan Yeah. Come on. Go. 對，來吧，開始。 Iris and Dan Okay, okay. I'm thinking. I'll start on A4. 好，好，我在想。我由 A4 開始。 Iris and Dan Okay. You're fine. Next move. 好，安全。下一步呢？ Iris and Dan I'll move forward one square, then move right two squares. 我向前一格，然後向右兩格。 Iris and Dan Gotcha. You've landed on my monster. 捉到你了！你走到我的怪物那格。 Iris and Dan Okay. So... 好吧，那…… Iris and Dan Your second life. 到你的第二條生命了。 Iris and Dan Right. My second life. Here goes. I'll start at A5. I move forward one square. 對，第二條生命。來吧，我由 A5 開始，向前一格。 Iris and Dan Now, um, I'll move left two squares. 然後，嗯，向左兩格。 Iris and Dan Okay. You're fine. 好，安全。 Iris and Dan Move forward three squares. And, and, move right one square. 向前三格，再、再向右一格。 Iris and Dan Okay. Here goes. Move forward one square. Did I make it? 好，來吧。向前一格。我成功了嗎？ Iris and Dan Yes. Well done, Dan. You made it. You survived the maze. 對，Dan，做得好！你成功了，活着走出了迷宮。 Iris and Dan Hooray! I won. No longer will I be called a loser. 萬歲，我贏了！再也沒有人可以叫我是失敗者。 Iris and Dan Well, I don't know about that. 這個我可不敢肯定。 Narrator Part C. Listen to Iris and Dan's discussion and answer the questions. 丙部分：聆聽 Iris 和 Dan 的討論，並回答問題。 Narrator Please note, you do not have to answer in full sentences. 請注意，你不需要用完整句子作答。 Iris and Dan So, what do you think? Any suggestions? 你覺得怎樣？有什麼建議？ Iris and Dan Hmm. Well, the grid's a bit boring to look at. You need to make the game look more colorful. 嗯，格子看起來有點沉悶。你要讓遊戲的色彩更豐富。 Iris and Dan Yes. It does look a bit boring. You're right. I'll ask Gabby in graphics to make it more 對，看起來是有點沉悶。你說得對，我會請美術部的 Gabby 把它設計得更 Iris and Dan colorful. And I'd suggest having more monsters. That'll make it more challenging. 繽紛。我也建議加入更多怪物，這樣會更有挑戰性。 Iris and Dan Yes. I suppose adding more monsters would make it more fun too. 對，我想加入更多怪物也會更有趣。 Iris and Dan But I have a question. I was just wondering how will people actually play it online? The game, 不過我有一個問題：大家究竟怎樣在網上玩這個遊戲？ Iris and Dan I mean. Well, we're going to allow two ways of playing the game. The first one is by 我是指實際玩法。我們會提供兩種玩法。第一種是 Iris and Dan actually speaking like we did. Oh, that's quite cool. So, you speak to your smartphone 像我們剛才那樣直接說出指令。很酷。即是你對着智能手機說話， Iris and Dan and it marks your route on the grid? Yes, that’s right. All voice controlled. 它就會在格子上標示你的路線？沒錯，全靠語音控制。 Iris and Dan The second way is that you can simply touch the screen. 第二種方式就是直接觸碰螢幕。 Iris and Dan Yes. I can imagine this working well with like touch screen devices like smartphones. 對，我能想像它很適合智能手機這類觸控螢幕裝置。 Iris and Dan But how can people be sure that the game's not cheating and, you know, 但大家怎樣確定遊戲沒有作弊，沒有在 Iris and Dan just placing the monsters after the player makes a move? 玩家走完一步後才放置怪物？ Iris and Dan This is the tricky part. It's done in steps. So, in the first step, when the game starts, 這是比較棘手的部分，要分步驟進行。第一步，遊戲開始時， Iris and Dan the game sends a document to the player's phone. 遊戲會把一份文件傳送到玩家的手機。 Iris and Dan Okay. So, what happens after that? 好，之後呢？ Iris and Dan Right. The second step is that when the game's over, a password appears on the screen. 第二步，遊戲結束時，螢幕上會出現一組密碼。 Iris and Dan Okay. Right. And then, what's the password for? 好，那密碼有什麼用途？ Iris and Dan Right. So, the third step is that the player opens the document with the password. 第三步，玩家用該密碼開啟文件。 Iris and Dan Okay. Cool. So, they open the document in the third step. 明白，很好。他們在第三步開啟文件。 Iris and Dan Then the fourth and final step is that the player checks the location of the monsters. 第四步，也是最後一步，玩家檢查怪物的位置。 Iris and Dan Okay. That is clever. So, when the player checks the location, 很聰明。玩家檢查位置後， Iris and Dan he knows then that the game hasn't been cheating. 就知道遊戲沒有作弊。 Iris and Dan Exactly. 正是。 Narrator That is the end of task two. You now have one minute to tidy up your answers. 任務二完結。你現在有一分鐘整理答案。 怪物迷宮 Iris 正在為下一期雜誌製作網上遊戲。任務二分三部分：甲部分，Iris 向 Dan 解釋玩法；乙部分，Dan 玩遊戲；丙部分，Dan 和 Iris 討論遊戲。 甲部分——怪物迷宮圖例 在怪物迷宮圖例所提供的空格填上缺漏資料。 例子：迷宮橫列由下至上為 A–F，直欄為 1–6。灰色格子：E4、D1、C5、B2。示範標記：A4、B4、B3、C3、D3、E3 為 O；E2 為 M。 方向：↑ 向前；← 向左；→ 向右；↓ 向後。 灰色格子＝ O＝走過的路線。 M＝走到隱藏怪物所在的格子。 乙部分 按照上方怪物迷宮圖例的示範，在 Dan 走過的每一格畫圓圈（O），標示他的路線；如遇上隱藏怪物，則填 M。 Dan 的第一條生命。請在格子上標示路線；灰色格子是 E6、D1、B2。 Dan 的第二條生命。請在格子上標示路線；灰色格子是 E1、E6、D1、B2。 丙部分 聆聽 Iris 和 Dan 的討論，回答問題。毋須用完整句子作答。 Dan 對改善怪物迷宮遊戲有什麼建議？ 大家會如何在網上玩這個遊戲？ 玩家怎樣確信遊戲沒有在放置怪物時作弊？ 第一，遊戲開始時， 。 第二，遊戲結束時， 。 第三， 。 第四， 。
