entries.text: Kaity is at the airport. She is calling Dan to ask him to edit an article she has been working on. There are three parts to Task 3. In Part A, you have to correct some sentences. In Part B, you have to provide labels for parts of a painting and in Part C you have to complete a text. Part A Each line of the text below may have one mistake. Correct the mistake. If the line is correct then put a tick ✓ in the right-hand column. Corrections Sentence Correction / ✓ “Children’s Games” is one of the most famous drawings to show children playing. paintings (example) It was started in the year 1560. The artist who created it was called Pete Bruegel the Elder. He was born in the Netherlands and died in Belgium. Part B Label the four games the children are playing in the painting. Use no more than FOUR words for each. Upper circle Right circle Small left circle Large lower circle Part C Complete the text. Write one or more words in each gap. Pixel-art examples based on classic paintings One kind of contemporary video game is based on classic works of art. Most of these games use because the game designers enjoy the challenge of using with to make . The games are simple and their intention is to be . These games can be played online . Narrator Three. Katie is at the airport. She is calling Dan to ask him to edit an article she has been working 任務三。Kaity 在機場，正打電話給 Dan，請他編輯她一直在撰寫的文章。 Narrator on. There are three parts to task three. In part A, you have to correct some sentences. 任務三分為三部分。甲部分，你要改正一些句子。 Narrator In part B, you have to provide labels for parts of a painting. 乙部分，你要為畫作中指定的部分加上標籤。 Narrator And in part C, you have to complete a text. 丙部分，你要完成一段文字。 Narrator You now have 30 seconds to study task three. At the end of the task, 你現在有三十秒閱讀任務三。本任務結束後， Narrator you will have one minute to tidy up your answers. Part A. Each line of the text below 你將有一分鐘整理答案。甲部分：下面文字的每一行 Narrator may have one mistake. Correct the mistake as shown below. If the line is correct, 可能有一個錯誤。請按下方示範改正錯誤。如果該行正確， Narrator then put a tick in the right-hand column. The first has been provided as an example. 在右欄加上剔號。第一項已作為例子提供。 Kaity and Dan Hello. 喂。 Kaity and Dan Oh, hi, Dan. 你好，Dan。 Kaity and Dan Hi. Where are you? 你好，你在哪裡？ Kaity and Dan I'm at the airport. Look, Dan, I've written this article about games and art, 我在機場。Dan，我寫了一篇關於遊戲與藝術的文章， Kaity and Dan but didn't have time to finish editing it. And like an idiot, I forgot my laptop. 但沒時間完成編輯。我真笨，竟然忘了帶手提電腦。 Kaity and Dan I need you to check some things for me. Can you open up the file? It's in the Dropbox folder. 我需要你替我核對一些資料。你能開啟檔案嗎？在 Dropbox 資料夾裡。 Kaity and Dan Sure. Okay. Let me just open it up. Right. I'm ready. 當然，讓我開啟它。好，準備好了。 Kaity and Dan Okay. At the start of the article, I discuss a famous painting called 文章開頭，我討論一幅著名畫作，叫 Kaity and Dan Children's Games by Peter Bruegel, the Elder. 老布魯蓋爾的《兒童遊戲》。 Kaity and Dan It says here that it is a drawing. 這裡寫的是一幅素描。 Kaity and Dan That should be a painting. Can you change it? 應該是繪畫作品，你可以改一下嗎？ Kaity and Dan Okay. Done. 好，改好了。 Kaity and Dan Okay. Now, can you double check some of the facts are written correctly? 現在可以再核對一些資料有沒有寫對嗎？ Kaity and Dan I might have got the dates wrong, so please change it to 1560 if that's printed incorrectly. 年份可能寫錯了。如果不正確，請改成 1560 年。 Kaity and Dan No, no, it's right. You say here that it was started in 1560. 不，年份沒錯。你這裡寫的是 1560 年開始創作。 Kaity and Dan Ah, just as well you said that. It was completed then. 幸好你提起，應該是在那一年完成。 Kaity and Dan Oh, and check that I've spelled the artist's first name right. 還有，檢查我有沒有拼對畫家的名字。 Kaity and Dan It should be Pieter Bruegel and Pieter spelled P-I-E-T-E-R. 應該是 Pieter Bruegel，Pieter 的拼法是 P-I-E-T-E-R。 Kaity and Dan Oh, you've actually written Pete Bruegel. P-E-T-E. 噢，你其實寫成了 Pete Bruegel，P-E-T-E。 Kaity and Dan Thought so. 果然如此。 Kaity and Dan Okay. Let me just change that now. Okay. 好，讓我現在改過來。好了。 Kaity and Dan Right. And make sure I've got the countries right. I can never remember where he was born and died. 也請確定國家寫對了，我總記不住他在哪裡出生和去世。 Kaity and Dan He died in Belgium and was born in the Netherlands. Got it? 他在比利時去世，在荷蘭出生。明白嗎？ Kaity and Dan Yeah, I think so. 嗯，應該明白。 Kaity and Dan Okay. Now, the next thing is that I've put some labels on the painting 下一件事：我在畫上加了一些標籤， Kaity and Dan to point out interesting details about what the children are actually doing. 指出孩子們究竟在做什麼，展示一些有趣的細節。 Kaity and Dan Um, the games they're playing, I mean. I didn't manage to finish them. 我是指他們玩的遊戲。我還未完成標籤。 Kaity and Dan Could you add them as I go through them? 我逐項說明時，你可以替我補上嗎？ Kaity and Dan Yes, let's see. I've got the picture up here now. 可以，讓我看看，圖片已經開啟了。 Kaity and Dan So, if you look closely, there's one boy sitting cross-legged on the grass. 仔細看，有個男孩盤腿坐在草地上。 Kaity and Dan Well, this was actually a form of exercise at the time, a bit like yoga today. 這其實是當時的一種運動，有點像今天的瑜伽。 Kaity and Dan Okay. I can see that now. It does look like he's doing a yoga exercise. 現在看到了，確實很像在做瑜伽運動。 Kaity and Dan I didn't realise before. 我之前沒有留意到。 Kaity and Dan Also, in the picture, there are girls holding a basket. 畫裡還有一些女孩拿着籃子。 Kaity and Dan Oh yes, I see them. Seems to be a basket of fruit or something. 對，看到了，好像是一籃水果之類的。 Kaity and Dan So, what are they doing then? It doesn't look like a game. 那她們在做什麼？看起來不像遊戲。 Kaity and Dan Well, they're actually performing a wedding, a pretend wedding. 她們其實在扮演婚禮，是假裝的婚禮。 Kaity and Dan Oh, I remember having to dress up for pretend weddings when I was little with my big sister. 我記得小時候要跟姐姐打扮好，玩扮婚禮的遊戲。 Kaity and Dan Oh, now that would be a wedding picture I'd love to see. 那可真是我很想看的一張婚禮照片。 Kaity and Dan Yeah, well. 嗯，好吧。 Kaity and Dan Now, what else? Okay, you see those boys on top of the fence? 還有什麼呢？你看到坐在圍欄上的男孩嗎？ Kaity and Dan Well, they're playing at riding horses. 他們在假裝騎馬。 Kaity and Dan Oh yes, I can see that now. They really do look like they are riding a horse. 對，現在看出來了。他們真的很像在騎馬。 Kaity and Dan So, what about the kids jumping over the other kids' legs? 那些跳過其他孩子雙腿的孩子又在做什麼？ Kaity and Dan What's that about? 那是什麼遊戲？ Kaity and Dan This game's actually quite painful. 這個遊戲其實很痛。 Kaity and Dan The children would apparently kick very hard and it would really hurt. 據說孩子們會很用力踢，真的會令人受傷。 Kaity and Dan Ouch! So, it's a kicking game. 哎喲，所以是踢人的遊戲。 Kaity and Dan I'm glad we didn't play that when I was at school. 幸好我上學時沒有玩這個。 Kaity and Dan We did something similar, actually. 其實我們也做過類似的事。 Kaity and Dan Kicking people, I mean. It was quite violent. 我是指踢人，相當暴力。 Kaity and Dan Really? 真的嗎？ Narrator Part C. Complete the text. 丙部分：完成這段文字。 Narrator Write one or more words in each gap. 每個空格填上一個或多個字。 Kaity and Dan Right, moving on. What else is there? 好，繼續，還有什麼？ Kaity and Dan Oh, oh yes. At the end of the article, there's a section on present-day games. 對了，文章末段有一節談今天的遊戲。 Kaity and Dan Games that use classic art for their graphics. 就是用經典藝術作品作為畫面的遊戲。 Kaity and Dan I didn't quite finish that. 那一部分我還未寫完。 Kaity and Dan Oh, okay. They look fun. 好，看起來很有趣。 Kaity and Dan Yeah, I loved reading up on this. 是啊，我很喜歡閱讀這方面的資料。 Kaity and Dan I like the fact that they're making a video game out of a classic work of art 我很喜歡他們把經典藝術作品改編成電子遊戲， Kaity and Dan like The Last Supper or The Mona Lisa. 例如《最後的晚餐》和《蒙娜麗莎》。 Kaity and Dan Yeah, I know. They're brilliant, aren't they? 對，真的很棒。 Kaity and Dan So, what's interesting is that these games use 8-bit graphics. 有趣的是，這些遊戲使用八位元圖像。 Kaity and Dan 8-bit? You mean like early computer graphics? 八位元？你是指早期的電腦圖像嗎？ Kaity and Dan Why use 8-bit graphics? That's a bit weird. 為什麼用八位元圖像？這有點奇怪。 Kaity and Dan Well, because for the game designers, it's a challenge. 因為對遊戲設計師來說，這是一個挑戰。 Kaity and Dan They're trying to use these little blocks with only a few colours to create very complex pictures. 他們嘗試用這些小方塊和少量顏色，製作非常複雜的圖畫。 Kaity and Dan Hmm. 嗯。 Kaity and Dan What I mean is that they, the designers of these computer games, 我的意思是，這些電腦遊戲的設計師 Kaity and Dan enjoy making these really complicated images from small blocks using only a small number of colours. 很享受只用小方塊和少量顏色，製作非常複雜的圖像。 Kaity and Dan Yeah, okay. Well, let me just finish making a note of that. 好，讓我先把這一點記下。 Kaity and Dan Right, keep going. 好，繼續。 Kaity and Dan So, the games themselves are actually quite simple, like really, really simple, 遊戲本身其實相當簡單，真的非常、非常簡單， Kaity and Dan and there's a reason for that. 而這是有原因的。 Kaity and Dan And what's the reason? 什麼原因？ Kaity and Dan Well, these games are not meant to be serious. They're just supposed to be funny. 這些遊戲不是要讓人認真對待，只是想令人發笑。 Kaity and Dan You mean humorous funny, not weird funny? 你指幽默的「有趣」，不是古怪的「奇怪」？ Kaity and Dan Yeah, exactly, like a joke. 沒錯，就像一個笑話。 Kaity and Dan And where can you find these games? Do you have to pay for them? 在哪裡可以找到這些遊戲？要付錢嗎？ Kaity and Dan You can get them on the internet. The good thing is they're free. 在網上就找得到，好處是免費。 Kaity and Dan You don't need to pay anything. 一分錢也不用付。 Kaity and Dan Free? Well, that makes a change. 免費？這倒是難得。 Kaity and Dan Maybe I'll check them out. Is that everything? 我可能會去看看。都處理好了嗎？ Kaity and Dan Yes, that's all. Thanks for helping out, Dan. 對，就是這些。Dan，謝謝你幫忙。 《兒童遊戲》 Kaity 在機場，打電話請 Dan 編輯她一直在撰寫的文章。任務三分三部分：甲部分改正句子；乙部分為畫作指定部分加上標籤；丙部分完成文字。 甲部分 以下文字每行可能有一個錯誤。請改正錯誤；如果該行正確，在右欄加上剔號 ✓。 改正表格：句子／改正或 ✓。 《兒童遊戲》是描繪小孩玩樂的最著名「素描」之一。改正：繪畫作品（例子）。 它於 1560 年開始創作。 創作它的藝術家名為 Pete Bruegel the Elder。 他在荷蘭出生，在比利時去世。 乙部分 為畫作中的四款兒童遊戲加上標籤，每項不多於四個英文字。 上方圓圈： ；右方圓圈： 。 圖中為《兒童遊戲》的四組圈選人物。 左方小圓圈： ；下方大圓圈： 。 丙部分 完成文字。每個空格填上一個或多個字。 以經典畫作改編的像素藝術遊戲圖例。 有一類現代電子遊戲以經典藝術作品為基礎。大部分這類遊戲使用 ，因為設計師享受用 搭配 去製作 的挑戰。 這些遊戲很簡單，目的是 。它們可以在網上 玩。

entries.title: The psychology of games and play
entries.text: You will listen to the What, Why, How weekly podcast. Kaity is discussing the psychology of games and play with two professors of psychology. Answer the questions below and complete the table. What are the three key aspects mentioned in the definition of a game? Which point do Jonathan and Natalie disagree about? Complete the table Animal Type of Play Benefits Ants play fighting Fish What three key points does Natalie make about rats play fighting? First point: Second point: Third point: What do the rats learn from play fighting? Narrator You now have 30 seconds to study the task. 你現在有三十秒閱讀題目。 Narrator At the end of the task, you will have three minutes to tidy up your answers. 本任務結束後，你將有三分鐘整理答案。 Podcast discussion Hi. Well, today I'm joined by Dr Jonathan Newman from the University of Jeong Yi An. 你好，今天與我一起的有來自 Jeong Yi An 大學的 Jonathan Newman 博士。 Podcast discussion Good morning. 早安。 Podcast discussion And Dr Natalie Sum from the University of Eastern Australia. 還有東澳洲大學的 Natalie Sum 博士。 Podcast discussion Good morning, Katie. 早安，Kaity。 Podcast discussion Our discussion today is about the psychology of games and play. 今天我們會討論遊戲與玩樂的心理學。 Podcast discussion So let's dive in, shall we? 那就直接開始吧。 Podcast discussion Can we define what a game is, first of all? Jonathan? 首先，可以定義什麼是遊戲嗎？Jonathan？ Podcast discussion Help. That's a challenge. 哎呀，這是個挑戰。 Podcast discussion Well, we may say that most games have at least two key aspects in common. 我們可以說，大部分遊戲至少有兩個共同的主要特點。 Podcast discussion First, they provide some form of entertainment. 第一，它們提供某種形式的娛樂。 Podcast discussion We seek out games primarily for pleasure and fun. 我們主要為了快樂和趣味而玩遊戲。 Podcast discussion The second thing is that they seem to have some outcome or goal. 第二，它們似乎都有某種結果或目標。 Podcast discussion For instance, you either win or lose a game or finish it in some way. 例如，你不是贏就是輸，或者以某種方式完成遊戲。 Podcast discussion Would you agree with that, Natalie? Natalie，你同意嗎？ Podcast discussion Yes, Jonathan. 同意，Jonathan。 Podcast discussion Well, it's certainly true that games are primarily for entertainment 遊戲主要用來娛樂，這當然沒錯， Podcast discussion and that games all have some kind of outcome. 而且遊戲都有某種結果。 Podcast discussion I would like to add a third aspect. 我想加入第三個特點。 Podcast discussion Would you agree with me that games must follow some set of rules, too? 你同意遊戲也必須遵守一套規則嗎？ Podcast discussion Yes, I'd agree that following rules would be an essential element of games in general. 同意，總的來說，遵守規則是遊戲的重要元素。 Podcast discussion You know, Jonathan, to me, what's most fascinating is how games and life are so similar. Jonathan，對我而言，最有趣的是遊戲和人生如此相似。 Podcast discussion I'd even say life itself is but a game. 我甚至會說，人生本身不過是一場遊戲。 Podcast discussion Life is a game? 人生是一場遊戲？ Podcast discussion I hope you don't actually mean that. 希望你不是認真的。 Podcast discussion But it is, is it not? 但事實不就是這樣嗎？ Podcast discussion Life is simply a game we all have to play. 人生只是一場我們都必須參與的遊戲。 Podcast discussion Maybe your life's a game, Natalie. 也許你的人生是遊戲，Natalie， Podcast discussion Mine isn't. 我的可不是。 Podcast discussion And I don't think anyone else's is either. 我也不認為其他人的人生是遊戲。 Podcast discussion Actually, not even yours. 其實連你的也不是。 Podcast discussion Jonathan, your problem is you need to get some more fun in life. Jonathan，你的問題是需要在人生中多找點樂趣。 Podcast discussion I mean... 我是說…… Podcast discussion Okay, let's leave that point there. 好，這個話題就先談到這裡。 Podcast discussion Now, both of you have done a great deal of research into games and play in animals. 你們都對動物的遊戲與玩樂做了很多研究。 Podcast discussion Would you like to give some examples? 可以舉些例子嗎？ Podcast discussion Sure. 可以。 Podcast discussion Well, here's something that'll surprise you. 有一件事你一定會驚訝。 Podcast discussion Do you know ants play fight? 你知道螞蟻也會玩打鬥遊戲嗎？ Podcast discussion No, really? 不會吧，真的嗎？ Podcast discussion Ants? 螞蟻？ Podcast discussion Oh, yes. 對。 Podcast discussion That's right. 沒錯。 Podcast discussion It helps them fight better. 這有助牠們提升打鬥能力。 Podcast discussion It's really true. 是真的。 Podcast discussion That's incredible. 不可思議。 Podcast discussion So they actually get better at real fighting from play fighting. 所以牠們透過打鬥遊戲，能在真正打鬥時表現得更好。 Podcast discussion Here's another one that gets me. 另一個讓我驚訝的例子， Podcast discussion Fish play. 是魚也會玩樂。 Podcast discussion You know, sometimes when you're watching fish in a pond 有時你看着池塘裡的魚， Podcast discussion and they suddenly jump out for no apparent reason. 牠們會毫無明顯原因地突然跳出水面。 Podcast discussion Yeah, I've seen that. 對，我見過。 Podcast discussion I thought they'd jump to catch food. 我還以為牠們跳起來是為了捕捉食物。 Podcast discussion No, no, they jump for the fun of it. 不，牠們只是為了好玩而跳。 Podcast discussion Most fish feed underwater. 大部分魚在水底覓食。 Podcast discussion But this play jumping helps them in certain situations 不過，這種跳躍遊戲在某些情況下能幫助牠們， Podcast discussion like if they have to escape something trying to eat them. 例如逃避想吃掉牠們的東西。 Podcast discussion Yes, apparently jumping helps them escape from predators and hunters. 對，據說跳躍有助牠們逃離捕食者和獵捕者。 Podcast discussion But to me, what's really fascinating is how playing games 不過，對我而言真正有趣的，是玩遊戲 Podcast discussion actually develop morality in all kinds of animals. 怎樣讓各種動物發展出道德觀念。 Podcast discussion Can you give an example? 可以舉個例子嗎？ Podcast discussion Well, rats often engage in play fighting games. 老鼠經常玩打鬥遊戲。 Podcast discussion There are three points to note here. 這裡有三點值得留意。 Podcast discussion First, play fighting games occur between stronger and weaker rats. 第一，打鬥遊戲發生在較強壯和較弱小的老鼠之間。 Podcast discussion So one rat will always be stronger than another rat. 即是總有一隻老鼠比另一隻強壯。 Podcast discussion Precisely. 沒錯。 Podcast discussion I mean, the same is true in any kind of game. 其實任何遊戲都一樣。 Podcast discussion Someone will always be a bit better or a bit worse than the other player. 總會有人比對手略強或略弱。 Podcast discussion Now, the second point is where it gets interesting. 第二點就有趣了。 Podcast discussion If the weaker rat always loses, it will stop playing. 如果較弱的老鼠每次都輸，牠便會停止參與。 Podcast discussion You mean the weaker rat says, 你是說，較弱的老鼠會說， Podcast discussion right, I'm not playing this game if you keep winning. 「你老是贏，那我不玩了。」 Podcast discussion That's how I feel when I play scrabble or chess with my daughter. 我跟女兒玩拼字遊戲或國際象棋時，就是這種感覺。 Podcast discussion Now, for the third and most interesting part, 第三點，也是最有趣的一點， Podcast discussion the stronger rat learns that it has to let the weaker rat win 是較強的老鼠學會必須讓較弱的老鼠 Podcast discussion some of the time so they can keep playing. 有時也能贏，這樣大家才可以繼續玩。 Podcast discussion Oh, so the stronger rat will deliberately lose to the weaker rat. 所以較強的老鼠會故意輸給較弱的老鼠。 Podcast discussion Otherwise, it'll have no friends to play with. 否則牠就沒有朋友跟牠玩。 Podcast discussion Oh, poor strong rat with no friends. 可憐的強壯老鼠，沒有朋友。 Podcast discussion So I guess they are learning something very important from this. 我想牠們由此學到非常重要的東西。 Podcast discussion Absolutely. 絕對是。 Podcast discussion For one thing, they are developing a kind of morality. 一方面，牠們發展出某種道德觀念。 Podcast discussion The second thing is that they learn how to live together peacefully. 另一方面，牠們學會怎樣和平共處。 Podcast discussion Wow, that's amazing. 嘩，真神奇。 Podcast discussion So rats have to learn to be moral 所以老鼠要學習有道德， Podcast discussion and they have to learn how to live peacefully with one another, 也要學習彼此和平共處， Podcast discussion just like us humans have to do. 就跟我們人類一樣。 Podcast discussion That's absolutely fascinating. 這實在非常有趣。 Podcast discussion Okay, well, we're going to have a short break. 好，我們先稍作休息。 Podcast discussion And when we come back, 回來之後， Podcast discussion Natalie and Jonathan will be answering some of your questions. Natalie 和 Jonathan 會回答大家的一些問題。 Narrator That is the end of task four and of part 3a. 任務四及卷三甲部完結。 Narrator You now have three minutes to complete your answers to task four 你現在有三分鐘完成任務四的答案， Narrator and to tidy up all your other answers. 並整理所有其他答案。 遊戲與玩樂的心理學 你將聆聽《What, Why, How》每週播客。Kaity 正與兩位心理學教授討論遊戲與玩樂的心理學。回答下面的問題，並完成表格。 遊戲的定義中提及哪三個主要特點？ Jonathan 和 Natalie 在哪一點上意見不同？ 完成表格。欄目：動物／玩樂類型／好處。 螞蟻：打鬥遊戲； 。 魚： ； 。 Natalie 對老鼠的打鬥遊戲提出哪三個重點？ 第一點： 第二點： 第三點： 老鼠從打鬥遊戲中學會什麼？

entries.title: School mobile phone use policy
entries.text: Sarah is meeting with Ms Chan, the School Principal, and Ms Reyes, a Science teacher at the school, about the school’s mobile phone use policy. Listen to the discussion and write the information in the spaces below. The first one has been provided as an example. Summary of Meeting Topic of survey: Mobile phone use during the school day (example) Current policy Phones allowed (tick the correct option): until 8:30am until 8:45am until 8:55am Students’ opinions about mobile phone policy Current policy is Should be more Students’ requests for a new policy Total number of student responses to the survey: Most popular requests: Students want to use phones for at lunch time and when classes. Use in class Use in class Reason: Students want to use… Physics classes Language classes Ms Reyes and Ms Chan think phones should be used… Person Tick ONE option only Ms Reyes Ms Chan Other request from students Install a station Possible locations Possible locations Comments Corridor next to the playground Concerns about A good idea because Narrator Task 1. Sarah is meeting with Ms. Chan, the school principal, 任務一。Sarah 正與校長 Chan 女士 Narrator and Ms. Reyes, a science teacher at the school, about the school's mobile phone use policy. 和校內的科學科教師 Reyes 女士開會，討論學校的手機使用政策。 Narrator Listen to the discussion and write the information in the spaces below. 聆聽討論，並把資料寫在以下空格內。 Narrator The first one has been provided as an example. 第一項已作為例子提供。 Narrator You now have 30 seconds to study the task. 你現在有三十秒閱讀題目。 Narrator At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers. 本任務結束後，你將有一分鐘整理答案。 School policy discussion Good morning, Sarah. Come in. 早安，Sarah，請進。 School policy discussion I thought it would be useful to have Ms. Reyes here as well to hear about your survey. 我想也請 Reyes 女士在場，聽聽你的調查，會很有幫助。 School policy discussion Good morning, Sarah. Hello! Sarah，早安。你好！ School policy discussion Okay, so as I was saying, Ms. Reyes, Sarah and her team at our IT club online magazine have been doing a survey Reyes 女士，正如我剛才說，Sarah 和資訊科技學會網上雜誌的團隊正在進行調查， School policy discussion where they have been asking students about mobile phone use during the school day. 詢問學生在上課日使用手機的情況。 School policy discussion So Sarah, maybe you can give us some more details. Sarah，不如再詳細介紹一下。 School policy discussion Yes, and thank you for seeing me today. 好的，謝謝你們今天抽空見我。 School policy discussion Well, we're writing an article about the survey, 我們正在撰寫一篇關於這項調查的文章， School policy discussion and we thought it would be good to include your comments as well in the article. 也想把你們的意見加到文章裡。 School policy discussion Okay, fine. 好，沒問題。 School policy discussion The first issue we asked about was when we can use our phones during the school day. 我們首先問的是，上課日哪些時段可以使用手機。 School policy discussion At the moment, we're only allowed to use our phones until 8.45 in the morning. 目前，我們只可以用手機至早上八時四十五分。 School policy discussion And we can't use our phones during class. 上課時不能用手機。 School policy discussion Oh, I thought you could use your phones until 8.55. 噢，我還以為你們可以用到八時五十五分。 School policy discussion No, only until 8.45. 不，只可以用到八時四十五分。 School policy discussion Okay, my mistake. 好，是我弄錯了。 School policy discussion So students think the policy is outdated. 學生認為這項政策已經過時。 School policy discussion What do you mean by outdated? What would students like to change? 你說「過時」是什麼意思？學生想改變什麼？ School policy discussion Well, I think they'd like the policy to be more flexible. 我想他們希望政策更有彈性。 School policy discussion I see. And this is the feedback from the school survey you did. 明白，這是你們校內調查收集到的意見。 School policy discussion Sorry, can you tell us more about it? 不好意思，可以再多說一點嗎？ School policy discussion Yes, we did a survey to ask students about why they want to use their phones, 可以。我們透過調查詢問學生為什麼想使用手機， School policy discussion and lots of students responded. 有很多學生回應。 School policy discussion We heard from 64 junior students and 150 senior students, 我們收到六十四名初中生和一百五十名高中生的回覆， School policy discussion so that's 214 students in total. 即總共有二百一十四名學生。 School policy discussion 214? That's a lot of responses. 二百一十四？回應不少呢。 School policy discussion I'm impressed. Well done to the IT club. 令我印象深刻，資訊科技學會做得很好。 School policy discussion What were the main requests from students from the survey then? 那麼，調查中學生最主要的要求是什麼？ School policy discussion Well, the most popular requests were that students would like to use their phones 最多學生提出，希望可以使用手機， School policy discussion for 30 minutes at lunchtime and when walking between classes. 在午膳時段用三十分鐘，以及往返不同課堂的途中使用。 School policy discussion Walking between classes? Absolutely not. 往返課堂時？絕對不行。 School policy discussion Students would never arrive on time. 學生一定不能準時到達。 School policy discussion Half an hour at lunchtime is fair, but certainly not between classes. 午膳時用半小時算合理，但絕不能在往返課堂時使用。 School policy discussion There's just enough time and no more. 轉堂時間剛好夠用，沒有多餘時間。 School policy discussion Oh, okay. What else? 明白。還有什麼？ School policy discussion Oh yeah, they also said they'd like permission to use their phones 他們也希望獲准使用手機， School policy discussion during physics and language classes. 在物理和語文課上使用。 School policy discussion Why during those classes specifically? 為什麼特別是這兩類課堂？ School policy discussion Well, they'd like to use them in physics classes 他們想在物理課使用， School policy discussion so they can use calculator apps. 是為了用計算機應用程式。 School policy discussion And they want to use them in language classes for online dictionaries. 而在語文課則想用網上字典。 School policy discussion They said they think this would be really helpful for their studies, 他們認為這對學習很有幫助， School policy discussion especially for students who are preparing for exams. 尤其對準備考試的學生。 School policy discussion What do you think about that idea, Miss Reyes? Reyes 女士，你對這個想法有什麼看法？ School policy discussion Hmm. I don't agree that you need them in physics classes. 嗯，我不同意物理課需要用手機。 School policy discussion Scientific calculators are better than phone calculators, 科學計算機比手機計算機更好， School policy discussion but yes, they could be useful in language classes. 不過在語文課上，手機的確可能有用。 School policy discussion I think you're absolutely right about both points, Miss Reyes. Reyes 女士，你這兩點都說得完全正確。 School policy discussion There's no need to use phones during physics class, 物理課沒有必要使用手機， School policy discussion but using them for online dictionaries is definitely a good idea. 但用來查網上字典，的確是好主意。 School policy discussion Okay. Were there any other issues that came up from the survey? 好，調查中還有其他問題嗎？ School policy discussion Yes, there was one other request. 有，還有一項要求。 School policy discussion Students aren't allowed to charge their phone batteries in classrooms, 學生不能在課室為手機電池充電， School policy discussion so they'd like to ask for a battery charging station. 所以希望設置電池充電站。 School policy discussion A battery charging station. That's actually a good idea. 電池充電站，這其實是好主意。 School policy discussion Interesting. We'd have to think carefully about where to put it. 很有意思，但要仔細考慮放在哪裡。 School policy discussion Did they have any suggestions? The students, I mean. 學生有沒有提出位置建議？ School policy discussion Well, one place they said was, you know, in the corridor next to the playground. 他們提議其中一個位置，就是操場旁邊的走廊。 School policy discussion Hmm. I'm not so sure about that. 嗯，我對那裡有點保留。 School policy discussion There could be problems with security with that. 那裡可能有保安問題。 School policy discussion Yes, I tend to agree with Miss Chan, I'm afraid. 對，不好意思，我傾向同意 Chan 女士。 School policy discussion So that's out as a location then. But I still think it's a good idea. 那麼這個位置就不考慮了，但我仍覺得充電站是好主意。 School policy discussion Sarah, did you have another suggestion for a location? Sarah，你還有其他位置建議嗎？ School policy discussion The other one was the library. 另一個是圖書館。 School policy discussion Okay. Yeah, that might work. It's certainly popular at lunchtime. 好，那裡也許可行。午膳時確實很多人去。 School policy discussion Yeah, that's a good idea. We'll look into it definitely. 對，是好主意。我們一定會研究一下。 School policy discussion Okay. Well, I'll look forward to reading the article in the online magazine. 好，我期待在網上雜誌讀到這篇文章。 Narrator That is the end of task one. 任務一完結。 Narrator You now have one minute to tidy up your answers. 你現在有一分鐘整理答案。 校內手機使用政策 Sarah 正與校長 Chan 女士及校內科學科教師 Reyes 女士開會，討論學校的手機使用政策。聆聽討論，把資料填在以下空格。第一項已作為例子提供。 會議摘要 調查主題：在上課日（例子）使用手機。 現行政策 允許使用手機至何時？（選出正確選項並加剔號） A 上午八時三十分 B 上午八時四十五分 C 上午八時五十五分 學生對手機政策的意見 現行政策 。 政策應更 。 學生對新政策的要求 回覆問卷的學生總數： 。 最多人提出的要求：學生希望在午膳時使用手機 ，以及在 課堂時使用。 課堂使用情況。欄目：課堂／原因——學生想使用…… 物理課： 語文課： Reyes 女士和 Chan 女士認為手機應在哪些課堂使用？每人只選一項。 Reyes 女士： Chan 女士： 兩題選項相同：只在物理課／只在語文課／物理及語文課均可／任何課堂都不可以。 學生的其他要求 設置一個 站。 可能的位置。欄目：位置／意見。 操場旁邊的走廊：擔心 。 ：是好主意，因為 。

entries.title: Mentor Mine app
entries.text: Sarah is meeting with two other members of the IT Club, Aaron and Rachel, to discuss a new app that the school is going to promote to senior students. Listen to the discussion and write the information in the spaces below. The first one has been provided as an example. App name: Mentor (example) Mine Purpose of app Connect with students Get help with e.g. homework and Settings: Subject, level and mode Setting Details Subjects Any Starting levels Beginner, Apprentice and Modes — Academic Modes — Hobby Country and Example — Country Example — Specialism Office hours Time limit: and more on weekends. Reasons: To develop To show Feedback settings Setting Details More votes = Users can view Votes and messages from Narrator Task two. 任務二。 Narrator Sarah is meeting with two other members of the IT club, Aaron and Rachel, Sarah 正與資訊科技學會另外兩名成員 Aaron 和 Rachel 開會， Narrator to discuss a new app that the school is going to promote to senior students. 討論學校將向高中生推廣的一個新應用程式。 Narrator Listen to the discussion and write the information in the spaces below. 聆聽討論，並把資料填在以下空格內。 Narrator The first one has been provided as an example. 第一項已作為例子提供。 Narrator You now have 30 seconds to study the task. 你現在有三十秒閱讀題目。 Narrator At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers. 本任務結束後，你將有一分鐘整理答案。 Mentor Mine app discussion So we've been asked to give our views on this Mentor Mine app. 我們被請來評論這個 Mentor Mine 應用程式。 Mentor Mine app discussion You know, the one for senior students? 就是那個給高中生用的，你知道嗎？ Mentor Mine app discussion They want us to review it in the magazine. 他們想我們在雜誌裡寫一篇評測。 Mentor Mine app discussion I've had it on my phone and I've been giving it a go over the weekend. 我已經把它裝到手機上，週末試用了一下。 Mentor Mine app discussion What's it called? 它叫什麼名字？ Mentor Mine app discussion Mental Mine. Never heard of it. Mental Mine？沒聽過。 Mentor Mine app discussion Not mental. Mentor! 不是 Mental，是 Mentor！（更正名稱） Mentor Mine app discussion Let me show you. Wait a second till I find it on my phone. 我給你看看。等一下，讓我在手機上找出來。 Mentor Mine app discussion Right, here it is. 好，在這裡。 Mentor Mine app discussion Oh, okay. 噢，明白。 Mentor Mine app discussion Right, so it's an app and it helps you connect with other students from around the world. 這是一個讓你聯繫世界各地其他學生的應用程式。 Mentor Mine app discussion And so they help each other with things like homework and projects. 大家可以互相協助，例如做功課和專題研習。 Mentor Mine app discussion Oh, I've heard about this one. It's got really good reviews. 我聽過這個，評價很好。 Mentor Mine app discussion So you're saying you can get help with projects with this? 即是你可以用它獲得專題研習方面的幫助？ Mentor Mine app discussion Yeah, that's the idea anyway. 對，原意是這樣。 Mentor Mine app discussion Alright, so how do we get started? 好，怎樣開始？ Mentor Mine app discussion Can we have a look at the settings? 可以看看設定嗎？ Mentor Mine app discussion Right, settings. 好，設定。 Mentor Mine app discussion Right, here we go. You try it, Rachel. 來吧，Rachel，你試一下。 Mentor Mine app discussion Oh, okay. Right. 好，可以。 Mentor Mine app discussion So see the button with the head and the wheels. Press it. 你看到那個有人頭和齒輪的按鈕嗎？按下去。 Mentor Mine app discussion Well, here you start by choosing your subjects, your levels for each subject and your modes. 開始時在這裡選擇科目、每一科的程度，以及模式。 Mentor Mine app discussion You can select any subjects you like. 你可以選擇任何喜歡的科目。 Mentor Mine app discussion Oh, right. So it looks like there are three starting levels. 明白，看來有三個起始程度。 Mentor Mine app discussion Beginner, apprentice and guide. 初學者、學徒，以及嚮導。 Mentor Mine app discussion So presumably I'd select guide if I think I know like loads about a subject and beginner or apprentice if I don't. 所以如果我覺得自己對某科目很熟悉，就選嚮導；否則就選初學者或學徒。 Mentor Mine app discussion Exactly. 沒錯。 Mentor Mine app discussion What about mode? What does that mean? 模式又是什麼意思？ Mentor Mine app discussion Okay, well, press it. So you should see there are two modes. 按一下看看。應該會見到兩個模式。 Mentor Mine app discussion The first one is academic. See? 第一個是學術模式，看到了嗎？ Mentor Mine app discussion Oh, yeah. 看到了。 Mentor Mine app discussion You choose this one if you're preparing for an exam. 如果正在準備考試，就選這個。 Mentor Mine app discussion The other one is hobby and it's for like personal interest only. 另一個是興趣模式，只是為了個人興趣。 Mentor Mine app discussion Personal interest? Oh, so presumably people can talk about a subject even if, say, they're not studying for an exam? 個人興趣？所以即使不是為了考試，大家也可以討論某個科目？ Mentor Mine app discussion What's this one for? The one with the flag? Is that to choose my country? 這個有旗子的按鈕有什麼用？是選擇我的國家嗎？ Mentor Mine app discussion Let's try it. Right. 試一下吧。好。 Mentor Mine app discussion So it looks like there are two settings here, country and type of school. 看來這裡有兩個設定：國家和學校類型。 Mentor Mine app discussion But isn't it just for secondary schools? 但它不是只供中學使用嗎？ Mentor Mine app discussion Yeah, it is. But there are different types of schools in different countries, like many Italian schools specialising just one area. 對，不過不同國家有不同類型的學校，例如很多意大利學校只專門教授一個範疇。 Mentor Mine app discussion So if Italian teenagers want to specialise in, say, sports coaching, they can choose a school for that subject. 所以意大利青少年如果想專攻例如運動教練這一科，就可以選相關學校。 Mentor Mine app discussion Right. 明白。 Mentor Mine app discussion What's the clock for? Does it tell the time then? 時鐘有什麼用？顯示時間嗎？ Mentor Mine app discussion No, no. This is what they call the office hours setting. 不是，這叫「辦公時間」設定。 Mentor Mine app discussion You keeping up, Rachel? Rachel，跟得上嗎？ Mentor Mine app discussion Yeah, yeah, right. Office hours. Ah, because you're like a professor sitting in your office. That's clever. 跟得上。辦公時間，因為你就像坐在辦公室裡的教授，很聰明。 Mentor Mine app discussion So with this setting, you can choose your availability each day. 這個設定讓你選擇每天有空的時間。 Mentor Mine app discussion You can set a maximum of two hours each weekday to ask and answer live questions and more on weekends, say, three to four hours. 平日每天最多可設定兩小時，供即時提問和回答；週末則可以更多，例如三至四小時。 Mentor Mine app discussion You should set your office hours to when you would normally be doing your homework. 你應該把辦公時間設在平常做功課的時段。 Mentor Mine app discussion Why do they recommend to set time, do you think? 你覺得他們為什麼建議固定時間？ Mentor Mine app discussion Well, I was thinking about this and I think the first reason is they want to help students develop good time management skills. 我想過這個問題。第一個原因，是他們想幫助學生培養良好的時間管理能力。 Mentor Mine app discussion Yeah, I have no time management skills whatsoever. I'm such a deadline fighter. 對，我完全沒有時間管理能力，總是趕死線。 Mentor Mine app discussion Yeah, I know. And the other is that it's useful for other students to know exactly when you're available. 我知道。另一個原因是，讓其他學生清楚知道你何時有空，會很有用。 Mentor Mine app discussion Because if they know your availability, then they know when you might be able to answer a question. Makes sense. 他們知道你有空的時段，就知道你何時可能回答問題，這很合理。 Mentor Mine app discussion So what are these? What are they? Balloons or something? 這些又是什麼？氣球之類的東西？ Mentor Mine app discussion Yeah, I have no idea why. Anyway, you click this button to go to your feedback settings. 對，我不知道為什麼用這個圖案。不過按這個按鈕，就可以進入回饋設定。 Mentor Mine app discussion You see, each time you help someone, they can give you a vote and then write a message to say thanks. 每次你幫助別人，對方都可以投你一票，再寫留言表示感謝。 Mentor Mine app discussion The more votes you get, the sooner you can move up to a higher level. 得到的票越多，就越快能升到更高程度。 Mentor Mine app discussion OK. Yeah, it allows you to show or hide the number of votes you've got as well. 明白，也可以選擇顯示或隱藏所得票數。 Mentor Mine app discussion OK. Oh, and I can show or hide the messages I've received from people. You know, the ones that I've helped. That's pretty cool. 對，我還可以顯示或隱藏收到的留言，就是那些我幫過的人的留言，很不錯。 Mentor Mine app discussion Yeah, I know. I think it's pretty cool all round actually. 我也覺得整個應用程式都很好。 Mentor Mine app discussion Yeah, it looks useful. 對，看起來很有用。 Narrator That is the end of task two. You now have one minute to tidy up your answers. 任務二完結。你現在有一分鐘整理答案。 Narrator Task three. Sarah, Rachel and Erin are choosing stories about the use of technology around the world to feature in the IT Club's online magazine. 任務三。Sarah、Rachel 和 Aaron 正在挑選世界各地使用科技的故事，刊登於資訊科技學會網上雜誌。 Mentor Mine 應用程式 Sarah 正與資訊科技學會另外兩名成員 Aaron 和 Rachel，討論學校將向高中生推廣的新應用程式。聆聽討論，把資料填在以下空格。第一項已作為例子提供。 應用程式名稱：Mentor（例子）Mine。 應用程式的用途 聯繫 的學生。 取得協助，例如功課和 。 設定：科目、程度及模式。欄目：設定／詳情。 科目：任何科目。 起始程度：初學者、學徒及 。 模式——學術： 。 模式——興趣： 。 國家及 。 例子——國家： 。 例子——專修範疇： 。 辦公時間 時間上限： ；週末可以更多。 原因： 培養 。 顯示 。 回饋設定。欄目：設定／詳情。 更多票數＝ 。 用戶可以查看票數，以及來自 的留言。

entries.title: South Africa’s Youth Boost Centres
entries.text: Sarah, Rachel and Aaron are choosing stories about the use of technology around the world to feature in the IT Club’s online magazine. Listen to the information and complete the notes below. Story: South Africa’s Youth Boost Centres Two main reasons why people sign up: Youth Boost members are given called Imali. Two main ways to get Imali: Uses of Imali Places Uses In the centre Online Main reason users like the Youth Boost Centres: IT Club members’ views — Advantages of Youth Boost Centres Member View Rachel Aaron Possible disadvantages of Imali Member View Rachel Aaron Narrator Task three. Sarah, Rachel and Erin are choosing stories about the use of technology around the world to feature in the IT Club's online magazine. 任務三。Sarah、Rachel 和 Aaron 正在挑選世界各地使用科技的故事，刊登於資訊科技學會網上雜誌。 Narrator Listen to the information and complete the notes below. You now have 30 seconds to study the task. 聆聽資料並完成以下筆記。你現在有三十秒閱讀題目。 Narrator At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers. 本任務結束後，你將有一分鐘整理答案。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Right. So what stories have you found then, Rachel? Rachel，你找到什麼故事？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron OK, I'll go first. I was reading this interesting article about youth boost centres in South Africa that have been set up by the local government. 我先說吧。我看了一篇很有趣的文章，介紹南非由地方政府設立的 Youth Boost 青年支援中心。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron OK, so these youth boost centres, are they for teenagers? 這些青年支援中心是給青少年用的嗎？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Yeah, mainly for young people without a job and who aren't at college and they join the centre as members. 對，主要對象是沒有工作、也沒有讀大專的年輕人，他們會加入成為會員。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron So why do they sign up? 他們為什麼報名加入？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Well, they can learn loads of different things like the centres give them lots of practical advice on things like how to start their own companies. 他們可以學很多東西，例如中心提供大量實用建議，教他們怎樣創辦自己的公司。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Sounds good. I've always wanted to start my own company. I think I'd like that much more than a boring office job or something. 聽起來很好。我一直想開自己的公司，應該比沉悶的辦公室工作更合我心意。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Yeah, totally. Me too. They also help them learn new workplace skills, things like writing emails, that sort of thing. 完全同意，我也是。中心也幫助他們學習新的職場技能，例如寫電郵之類。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron It does sound good, but offering things like workplace skills, isn't that just like any other job centre? What's this got to do with technology? 聽起來不錯，但提供職場技能，不是跟其他就業中心一樣嗎？這跟科技有什麼關係？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Well, this one is special. The centres themselves are entirely cash free and young people who join can earn virtual money called imali, which means money in Zulu apparently. You can spend it there at the centre. 這裡很特別：中心完全不用現金，加入的年輕人可以賺取一種叫 Imali 的虛擬貨幣，據說在祖魯語中意思就是「錢」。可以在中心使用。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron So do they use computers to earn it, just like Bitcoin? 即是他們像比特幣那樣，用電腦賺取嗎？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron No, no. They earn this imali in lots of different ways. One of the things they can do is local volunteering and they can do any kind of volunteering as long as it's in the local area. 不是，他們可以用很多不同方式賺取 Imali，其中一種是參與本地義工服務；任何類型都可以，只要在附近地區進行。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Like they might help out a nearby school or help the old people in the community. The other thing they can do is go to personal development workshops. 例如協助附近學校或社區長者。另一個方法是參加個人成長工作坊。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron So they earn for attending. Yeah, that's nice. And what do they learn about at these workshops? 所以出席就能賺取，很不錯。他們在工作坊學什麼？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron You know, like how to not give up when you're dealing with a problem or how to set yourself goals, things like that. 例如遇到問題時怎樣不放棄，或怎樣為自己定目標之類。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron That sounds pretty cool. What can they buy with this? What's its name? 聽起來很棒。他們可以用這個——叫什麼名字？——買些什麼？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Imali. Imali（貨幣的名稱）。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Imali. Well, as I said, the centres are cash free, but they can use imali at the centre cafes to buy things like snacks. They can also use the money to pay for online courses. Imali。正如我所說，中心不用現金，但可在中心咖啡室用 Imali 買小食等東西，也可以用它支付網上課程費用。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Can they work on the courses at home too? 在家也可以修讀課程嗎？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron I think so, but the centres have computers so apparently most people prefer to spend time there. 應該可以，不過中心有電腦，所以大部分人似乎較喜歡留在那裡。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Sounds great. Anything else? I mean that they can buy with? 很好。還可以用它買什麼？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Imali. Yeah, the other online option is that you can donate imalis to charity. Imali。還有另一個網上用途，就是捐給慈善機構。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Does that mean the charity gets imalis? But how is that useful? 即是慈善機構收到 Imali？那有什麼用？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron No, no, the Youth Boost Centre gives the charities real money. 不是，青年支援中心會把真正的金錢交給慈善機構。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron But members, they don't earn actual money, but they still like it? 但會員沒有賺到真正的錢，也喜歡這裡？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Apparently so. 看來是。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron So what's the big attraction? 那最大的吸引力是什麼？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Well, from what it said in the article, it's just a place where they can feel a sense of belonging. 按照文章的說法，那是一個能讓他們感到歸屬感的地方。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Oh, that's really nice. Okay, so it would be good to write in the article what we think. Let's talk about the good points first. 真好。文章也應該寫寫我們的看法。先談優點吧。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Rachel, you were researching it. What do you reckon? Rachel，你做過資料搜集，你怎麼看？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron I think they're an excellent idea, mainly because they give people a way to give back to the community. So it's more than just basic welfare. 我覺得這是好主意，主要是給人機會回饋社會，因此不只是提供基本福利。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Yeah, I was thinking the same. What do you think, Aaron? 對，我也這樣想。Aaron，你覺得呢？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron From what Rachel was saying, I think the best thing seems to be that it lets people learn life skills, like having to deal with money. 從 Rachel 的介紹來看，我認為最好的是讓人學習生活技能，例如怎樣處理金錢。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Alright. What about the cons? Can you see any downsides to this imali system? 好，那缺點呢？你們看得出 Imali 制度有什麼不足嗎？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Well, the obvious problem that I can see is that actual money is more useful. 我看到最明顯的問題，是實際金錢更有用。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron People need real money to spend on meals, not just snacks, especially if they need to help their families. 大家需要真錢支付正餐，而不只是小食，尤其是需要幫補家計的人。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Yes, that's a very good point. What about you, Aaron? What do you think? 對，很有道理。Aaron，你又怎麼看？ Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Well, again, from what Rachel said so far, it's hard to see any bad points. 按 Rachel 到目前為止所說的，實在很難找出缺點。 Sarah, Rachel and Aaron Maybe the only downside I can think of would be it might be vulnerable to hacking. You know, because, well, someone could hack into it online. 也許唯一想到的不足，是它容易遭黑客入侵，因為有人可能透過網絡入侵系統。 Narrator That is the end of task three. You now have one minute to tidy up your answers. 任務三完結。你現在有一分鐘整理答案。 Narrator Four. Sarah is interviewing Dr. James Berg, a computer specialist working with the NGO Tarako Solutions for the IT Club's online magazine. 任務四。Sarah 正為資訊科技學會網上雜誌，訪問在非政府組織 Tarraco Solutions 工作的電腦專家 James Berg 博士。 南非 Youth Boost 青年支援中心 Sarah、Rachel 和 Aaron 正在挑選世界各地運用科技的故事，刊登於資訊科技學會網上雜誌。聆聽資料並完成以下筆記。 故事：南非 Youth Boost 青年支援中心 人們報名加入的兩個主要原因： Youth Boost 會員會獲得一種名叫 Imali 的 。 取得 Imali 的兩個主要方法： Imali 的用途。欄目：地方／用途。 中心內： 。 網上： 、 。 使用者喜歡青年支援中心的主要原因： 資訊科技學會成員的看法——青年支援中心的優點。欄目：成員／意見。 Rachel： 。 Aaron： 。 Imali 可能的缺點。欄目：成員／意見。 Rachel： 。 Aaron： 。

entries.title: Tarraco Solutions
entries.text: Sarah is interviewing Dr James Berg, a computer specialist working with the NGO Tarraco Solutions, for the IT Club’s online magazine. Listen to the interview and complete the answers below. You do not need to answer in complete sentences. Tarraco Solutions: A Summary In what kind of places does Tarraco Solutions work around the world? What problem did Tarraco Solutions recently solve by building a bus shelter in Thailand? According to Dr Berg, Tarraco Solutions values diversity. How is this shown in what they do? What are the two benefits of using AR technology that Dr Berg mentions? Why is AR training so important for some people in the community? Kerala, India: A Success Story What did the Kerala project aim to improve? Which two main problems did the team have to address in the Kerala project? According to Dr Berg, why did local people not trust the project at first? What benefits did the webcam live feed provide? Narrator Four. Sarah is interviewing Dr. James Berg, a computer specialist working with the NGO Tarako Solutions for the IT Club's online magazine. 任務四。Sarah 正為資訊科技學會網上雜誌，訪問在非政府組織 Tarraco Solutions 工作的電腦專家 James Berg 博士。 Narrator Listen to the interview and complete the answers below. Please note that you do not need to answer in complete sentences. 聆聽訪問，並完成以下答案。請注意，你不需要用完整句子作答。 Narrator You now have 30 seconds to study the task. At the end of the task, you will have three minutes to tidy up your answers. 你現在有三十秒閱讀題目。本任務結束後，你將有三分鐘整理答案。 Tarraco Solutions interview Dr. Berg, thank you for taking the time to meet us today. Can you tell us a bit about the ideas behind Tarako Solutions? Berg 博士，謝謝你今天抽時間見我們。可以介紹一下 Tarraco Solutions 背後的理念嗎？ Tarraco Solutions interview Certainly. Well, Tarako Solutions is an NGO, as you probably know, and we operate in poor and remote areas all over the world. 當然。你應該知道，Tarraco Solutions 是非政府組織，在世界各地貧困和偏遠地區工作。 Tarraco Solutions interview We work in these areas to solve local problems, infrastructure problems mainly. 我們在這些地方解決當地問題，主要是基建問題。 Tarraco Solutions interview Oh, really? That's quite interesting. What kind of infrastructure problems? 真的嗎？很有意思，是哪一類基建問題？ Tarraco Solutions interview Well, maybe I can illustrate what we do with a recent redevelopment project in Thailand we were working on, where we built a new bus shelter for a group of commuters. 讓我用最近在泰國進行的重建計劃作例子：我們為一群通勤者建了一個新巴士候車亭。 Tarraco Solutions interview This helped local people deal with an uncomfortable journey to work and school. 這幫助居民改善上班和上學路途不舒適的問題。 Tarraco Solutions interview And are the projects designed for special groups of people? 這些計劃是為某些特定群體設計的嗎？ Tarraco Solutions interview Actually, it's the opposite. We really try to embrace diversity in everything we do, so we always try to invite, you know, people who are often overlooked in traditional society. 其實正好相反。我們希望做每件事都能包容多元，所以常邀請傳統社會中容易被忽略的人參與。 Tarraco Solutions interview Very often it's these kind of people that don't get to have their say. 往往正是這些人，沒有機會表達意見。 Tarraco Solutions interview OK, now I'd like... 好，我想…… Tarraco Solutions interview Sorry, I was going to add. When we're building things like the bus shelter, we invite ideas from the children, 抱歉，我還想補充：興建巴士候車亭這類設施時，我們會徵求兒童的意見， Tarraco Solutions interview as they are the users who are often overlooked. 因為他們也是使用者，卻往往被忽略。 Tarraco Solutions interview Well, that all sounds very positive. I'd like to move on to how Tarako Solutions uses technology. 聽起來很積極。接下來想談談 Tarraco Solutions 怎樣使用科技。 Tarraco Solutions interview You work with AR, augmented reality. Is that right? 你們用的是 AR，擴增實境，對嗎？ Tarraco Solutions interview Yes, that's right. AR mixes digital elements with real life. 對，AR 把數碼元素與真實世界結合。 Tarraco Solutions interview It sounds quite technical. 聽起來很高深。 Tarraco Solutions interview It's the same tech used in the game Pokemon Go, but instead of a monster, you can see things like a new bridge or a staircase. 它跟《Pokémon Go》所用的科技一樣，只是你看見的不是怪物，而是新橋或樓梯之類。 Tarraco Solutions interview AR is great. I mean, we can literally see the designs as they would appear in real life. AR 很好用。我們能直接看見設計在現實中會呈現什麼樣貌。 Tarraco Solutions interview Amazing! 很神奇！ Tarraco Solutions interview And another thing about AR is that it lets other people see which final designs they like best. AR 另一個好處是，讓其他人看出自己最喜歡哪個最終設計。 Tarraco Solutions interview This is important because in order to choose the final design, we have a public vote. 這很重要，因為我們透過公眾投票選出最終設計。 Tarraco Solutions interview Right. Now, AR is new to me, so I imagine it is probably a new concept for most of the people you're dealing with. 明白。AR 對我而言很陌生，我想對大部分參與者也會是新概念。 Tarraco Solutions interview So how do you deal with that? 你們怎樣處理這個問題？ Tarraco Solutions interview Well, that's a good point. Everybody who's selected to join the project must attend a three-day AR training programme. 問得好。所有獲選參與計劃的人，都必須接受三天的 AR 培訓課程。 Tarraco Solutions interview OK. 明白。 Tarraco Solutions interview And for some users, it's actually the first time they've ever used a computer, so it's an essential part of the process. 有些人其實從未用過電腦，這是第一次，因此培訓是不可或缺的部分。 Tarraco Solutions interview Can you tell us what your favourite project has been so far? 到目前為止，你最喜歡哪個項目？ Tarraco Solutions interview Well, I think one of the most memorable developments has been the Kerala Project in India. 其中一個最難忘的發展項目，是印度的 Kerala 計劃。 Tarraco Solutions interview OK, and what did that entail? 那涉及什麼工作？ Tarraco Solutions interview Well, this was a project designed to improve a riverside path to a market. 計劃是改善一條通往市場的河邊小徑。 Tarraco Solutions interview There were several things we had to address. 我們要處理幾個問題。 Tarraco Solutions interview We had to build in safety measures into the design to help deal with flash floods, for a start. 首先，設計中要加入安全措施，應付突發洪水。 Tarraco Solutions interview That was important. 這很重要。 Tarraco Solutions interview Plus, one special thing about this project was that the children who used the route gave us important information. 另外，這個項目有一點特別：使用該路線的孩子給了我們重要資料。 Tarraco Solutions interview They, the children, told us that actually the area had a problem with a lot of dangerous pests, especially snakes. 孩子告訴我們，該區其實有很多危險的有害動物，尤其是蛇。 Tarraco Solutions interview So again, we built in features to deal with that. 因此我們也設計了應對這個問題的設施。 Tarraco Solutions interview Right. 明白。 Tarraco Solutions interview This project also taught us a lot about building trust. 這個項目也讓我們學到很多建立信任的方法。 Tarraco Solutions interview I mean, many of the locals were quite doubtful at first. 不少居民最初抱懷疑態度。 Tarraco Solutions interview Did they explain why? 他們有解釋原因嗎？ Tarraco Solutions interview Yes, they did. 有。 Tarraco Solutions interview They told us about a similar project in the village a few years before that had been left unfinished and actually never was finished. 他們說，幾年前村內有個類似項目半途停工，到最後也沒有完成。 Tarraco Solutions interview So I suppose they would have been worried that the same thing might happen to your project, that it wouldn't be finished either. 所以他們可能擔心同樣情況會在你們的項目發生，最終也不能完成。 Tarraco Solutions interview Precisely. 正是。 Tarraco Solutions interview Which I think is fair enough. 我覺得這很合理。 Tarraco Solutions interview I think it was a genuine concern. 這是切實的憂慮。 Tarraco Solutions interview The other reason why they were quite doubtful about it all was to do with what would happen after we left. 另一個令他們懷疑的原因，是我們離開後會怎樣。 Tarraco Solutions interview They were worried that there would be no one to maintain the path once we'd gone. 他們擔心我們走了，就沒有人保養那條小徑。 Tarraco Solutions interview Again, another genuine worry. So how did you change their minds? 又是一個實在的憂慮。你們怎樣改變他們的想法？ Tarraco Solutions interview Well, we had to convince them that we aren't just another temporary volunteer project, that we wouldn't just leave. 我們要說服他們，我們不是又一個短暫的義工計劃，不會就此離開不管。 Tarraco Solutions interview What really helped was another piece of technology, one that could continue to support the Kerala project long after construction had finished. 真正有幫助的是另一項科技，在建造完成很久之後，仍可以支援 Kerala 計劃。 Tarraco Solutions interview Oh yeah? And what was that? 是嗎？那是什麼？ Tarraco Solutions interview Well, we set up webcams that deliver a live feed 24 hours a day on our webpage. It’s a win-win for everyone. 我們架設了網絡攝影機，每天二十四小時在網站直播，對各方都是雙贏。 Tarraco Solutions interview It means that for the local users we can easily see areas where the path had deteriorated. 對當地使用者而言，我們可以輕易看出小徑哪些地方已經損壞。 Tarraco Solutions interview The webcams are great for that, so it's been a great success. 網絡攝影機在這方面很有效，所以相當成功。 Tarraco Solutions interview And for Turaco Solutions, what were the benefits? You said it was a win-win situation. 那對 Tarraco Solutions 有什麼好處？你說是雙贏。 Tarraco Solutions interview Oh yes, sorry. It also means that we at Turaco Solutions can get more funding as we promote our work online using the images. 對，不好意思。這也讓我們可以用影像在網上推廣工作，從而獲得更多資助。 Tarraco Solutions interview OK. Thank you so much for telling us about Turaco Solutions today. 好，非常感謝你今天介紹 Tarraco Solutions。 Tarraco Solutions Sarah 正為資訊科技學會網上雜誌，訪問在非政府組織 Tarraco Solutions 工作的電腦專家 James Berg 博士。聆聽訪問並完成以下答案。毋須用完整句子作答。 Tarraco Solutions：摘要 Tarraco Solutions 在世界各地哪一類地方工作？ Tarraco Solutions 最近在泰國興建巴士候車亭，解決了什麼問題？ Berg 博士說 Tarraco Solutions 重視多元。他們的工作怎樣體現這一點？ Berg 博士提到使用擴增實境（AR）科技的哪兩項好處？ 為什麼 AR 培訓對社區內某些人如此重要？ 印度 Kerala：一個成功故事 Kerala 計劃旨在改善什麼？ 團隊在 Kerala 計劃中要處理哪兩個主要問題？ 根據 Berg 博士，當地人最初為什麼不信任這個計劃？ 網絡攝影機直播帶來什麼好處？

Julia and Mark are looking at the web page of world watch travel. Now you can with World 你曾否想過成為探險家，發現新的動物？現在有 World Julia and Mark Watch Travel. With World Watch Travel you go on an eco-friendly adventure to a protected part Watch Travel 就能實現。參加 World Watch Travel，你會展開一趟環保歷險，前往受保護的 Julia and Mark of the Brazilian rainforest. Oh, it's in Brazil. Wow, it sounds amazing. When can we go? Well, 巴西雨林。原來在巴西，嘩，聽起來很棒。我們什麼時候可以去？嗯， Julia and Mark let me see. Hmm, it says here you can book an expedition in the summer and each one lasts for 讓我看看。這裡說夏季可以預訂考察團，每趟持續 Julia and Mark six nights. Do you wander around the rainforest by yourselves for six nights? No, you go in a group 六晚。即是自己在雨林裡逛六晚？不，是跟團， Julia and Mark and groups are made up of eight to ten students from different countries. Eight to ten students 每組由來自不同國家的八至十名學生組成。八至十名學生 Julia and Mark in a group. That's quite a lot. Safety in numbers, I suppose. Yeah, I suppose so. And wait, 一組，人數不少。我想人多比較安全吧。對，應該是。等等， Julia and Mark how much does it cost? Let's see. It says for students it's 750 US dollars. 要多少錢？看看，學生價是七百五十美元。 Julia and Mark How much is that in Hong Kong dollars? I think it's around 6,000 Hong Kong dollars. 換成港幣是多少？我想大約六千港元。 Julia and Mark 6,000? Well, it's not cheap but it's a holiday of a lifetime. All right, let's see what they actually 六千？雖然不便宜，但這是畢生難忘的假期。好，看看他們實際 Julia and Mark do. Can you click on main activity? Sure. Okay, so the main activity is studying small animals. 做什麼。你可以按「主要活動」嗎？可以。主要活動是研究小型動物。 Julia and Mark So what do we have to do? Well, it says here you will set up traps. Oh my goodness, 那我們要做什麼？這裡說要設置陷阱。天啊， Julia and Mark that means we have to catch real animals in traps and see what we find. I hope there are no big 那就是用陷阱捕捉真正的動物，看看抓到什麼。希望沒有大 Julia and Mark spiders. Okay, what do we do with the animals once they're in the traps? All right, let me read. 蜘蛛。動物進了陷阱後，我們要怎樣做？讓我讀讀看。 Julia and Mark So apparently we need to check their weight and general health. Right, so we check to see how 看來我們要檢查牠們的體重和整體健康狀況。即是看看 Julia and Mark much they weigh and also see if they're healthy. Sounds okay? Yeah, sounds fun. Hmm, what about 牠們有多重，也檢查是否健康。可以吧？可以，聽起來有趣。那 Julia and Mark facilities? What kind of facilities do they offer? Right, so it looks like you stay in a lodge and 設施呢？提供哪些設施？看來是住在小屋裡， Julia and Mark it looks like each lodge has a toilet at least and a shower. Well, that's good news. It's 每間小屋至少有廁所和淋浴設施。好消息。這…… Julia and Mark so is there a kitchen? Hmm, it doesn't look like it. So where are we supposed to cook, do you think? 有廚房嗎？看起來沒有。那我們要在哪裡煮食？ Julia and Mark That's what I was wondering. Hmm, but there is a lounge so you can hang out with the rest of 我也在想。不過有休息室，所以你可以跟 Julia and Mark your group in the lounge if you want to. Okay, that's good. Oh, but look, there's no hot water. 同組其他人在休息室聚一聚。很好。噢，但你看，沒有熱水。 Julia and Mark That can be very pleasant. I suppose the water is warm enough for a shower. Well, it all sounds 那也可以很舒服吧，我想水應該夠暖，可以洗澡。聽起來一切都很 Julia and Mark amazing even with cold water. Yeah, I agree. Oh, here's a map of the campsite locations. 棒，即使用冷水也是。對，我同意。這裡有營地位置地圖。 Julia and Mark You can see where there are interesting places and where new species have been found. Blue 你可以看到有哪些有趣的地方，以及在哪裡發現了新物種。藍色 Julia and Mark camps where the exploration starts is the most northern campsite. You can see here on the top 營地是考察的起點，也是最北面的營地，就在 Julia and Mark left of the map. They say a lot of new insects have been discovered here. The next one on the 地圖左上角。據說這裡發現了很多新昆蟲。清單上的下一個 Julia and Mark list is Red Camp. It's quite far away from Blue Camp on the other side of the map. Oh yes, 是紅色營地，離藍色營地相當遠，在地圖另一邊。對， Julia and Mark over here on the right. Yes, there's a veterinary center here, so that's where they take any sick 在右邊這裡。這裡有獸醫中心，他們會把發現的生病 Julia and Mark animals they find. This area is where new species of butterfly have been found. The next one's 動物帶到這裡。這一區曾發現新的蝴蝶品種。下一個是 Julia and Mark Green Camp. It's right in the middle of the map. It says you can often see turtles here. 綠色營地，在地圖正中央，這裡說經常可以看到龜。 Julia and Mark The last one's Yellow Camp. Over in the southeast. Is it because there 地區已經大約一年。是什麼吸引你們來這片海域？因為這裡 Jason and Dr Anita Carter are lots of endangered species here? No, actually no. Well, there's so much going on under the surface of the ocean. 發現了什麼嗎？海面之下有很多事情發生， Jason and Dr Anita Carter So much to find out. But I suppose the main discovery was a new species of snailfish. 也有很多值得發掘的東西。不過我想最主要的發現，是一個新的獅子魚品種。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter Snailfish? That's quite an unfortunate name. Yes, but they're a very special creature. 獅子魚？英文叫 snailfish，名字不太好聽呢。對，但牠們是非常特別的生物。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter I have a map here. It's not to scale, but it gives you an idea of where we found the fish. 這裡有一張地圖，並非按比例繪製，不過能讓你了解發現魚類的位置。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter Before, we could only go down to around 3,000 meters. Let's have a look. 我們也有找到的動物影像。好，一起看看。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter Okay, so this one here is the snailfish. They are long-legged isopods, 不，牠來自地球。這是我們拍到的另一種動物：長腿等足類動物， Jason and Dr Anita Carter and they're about the size of a human hand. They look a lot like spiders. They have very small 大小約有人類手掌那麼大，看起來很像蜘蛛。牠們的身體很小， Jason and Dr Anita Carter bodies and eight long, very thin legs. Yes, they do look like spiders. 有八條很長、很幼的腿。對，真的很像蜘蛛。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter The third interesting creature you can see here was a type of sea cucumber called a sea pig. 第三種有趣的生物，是一種叫「海豬」的海參。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter A sea pig? That's an even more unfortunate name than snailfish. 海豬？這名字比 snailfish 還要糟糕。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter Indeed, but again, they're quite special. This animal was observed in a different part of the 的確，但牠們同樣很特別。這隻動物是在海洋的另一個區域 Jason and Dr Anita Carter ocean, but we use the same technology to film it. They have several short legs on the underside 觀察到的，不過我們用相同科技拍攝。牠們身體下方有幾條短腿， Jason and Dr Anita Carter of their bodies, and usually four legs that extend from the top. This one has just two. 通常還有四條腿從身體上方伸出。不過這一隻只有兩條。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter You can see here that all these legs help them climb over rocks. 你可以看到，這些腿幫助牠爬過岩石。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter Yes, that's extraordinary. So those aren't antennae on the top of its head? 真奇妙。所以頭頂那些不是觸角？ Jason and Dr Anita Carter No, those are more legs. Right, let's go back to the snailfish. 不是，那也是腿。好，回到獅子魚。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter They look very fragile, are they? Well, they are very delicate animals, 牠們看起來很脆弱，是嗎？牠們的確非常柔弱， Jason and Dr Anita Carter but they do have hard parts. Actually, their teeth and ear bones are the hardest structures 但也有堅硬部分。事實上，牙齒和耳骨是牠們身體裡最硬的結構。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter in their bodies. Oh, that's interesting. I thought their spines would be the toughest part, 有趣，我還以為脊骨最硬， Jason and Dr Anita Carter as you can see them in the picture. So they have hard teeth, you say? 因為在圖片裡看得見。你說牠們有堅硬的牙齒？ Jason and Dr Anita Carter Yes, they use them to scare off other fish. 對，用來嚇退其他魚。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter Right. So I get it why they would need hard teeth. But why do they need ear bones? 明白為什麼需要硬牙齒了，但為什麼需要耳骨？ Jason and Dr Anita Carter Well, they need ear bones for balance, just as humans do. 牠們需要耳骨來保持平衡，就像人類一樣。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter So the ear bones help them stay upright in the water? 即是耳骨讓牠們在水中保持正直姿勢？ Jason and Dr Anita Carter Yeah, basically. Without the ear bones, they would have a hard time swimming in the right 基本上是。沒有耳骨，牠們便很難朝正確的 Jason and Dr Anita Carter direction. And what about the rest of their bodies? 方向游泳。那身體其他部分呢？ Jason and Dr Anita Carter Well, they're covered with a skin that looks a bit like jelly. 牠們表面覆蓋着一層看起來像啫喱的皮膚。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter This means that they cannot survive for long when they're brought to the surface. 這意味牠們被帶到水面後，無法存活很久。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter Why can't they survive? 為什麼不能存活？ Jason and Dr Anita Carter Well, it's really difficult to maintain the conditions they need to survive on the surface. 因為在水面很難維持牠們生存所需的條件。 Jason and Dr Anita Carter It's easy enough to make the tank dark and to give them the right kind of food, 把魚缸弄暗、提供合適食物，倒不困難， Jason and Dr Anita Carter but they need very cold temperatures and very high pressure. They believed they were well prepared for the journey, as they thought 沒有什麼好擔心。他們相信已為旅程作好準備，因為覺得 Julia, Mark and museum guide they had everything they would need. This meant that, although the ship got their order in time, 品質不太好。結果即使船隻準時收到貨， Julia, Mark and museum guide what they ended up with was a lot of bad food. Some of the canned vegetables were rotten. 收到的卻是一大堆劣質食物，有些罐頭蔬菜已經腐爛。 Julia, Mark and museum guide Some of the meat would have been OK for animals, but not for people. Previously, 有些肉可能可以餵動物，卻不適合人吃。過去 Julia, Mark and museum guide experts thought that the cans had been made with dangerous metals, but we now know that 專家以為罐子使用了危險金屬，但現在我們知道 Julia, Mark and museum guide that isn't true. That wasn't the problem. So, is that how they died? Well, we know that 那不是真的，問題不在此。那他們就是因此死去？我們知道， Julia, Mark and museum guide the ship became trapped in ice, and most experts believe that it remained trapped there for three 船被困在冰裡，大部分專家相信，足足被困了三個 Julia, Mark and museum guide winters. Most experts think they were there for three winters. Does that mean no one's really 冬天。大部分專家認為三個冬天，即是沒有人真正 Julia, Mark and museum guide sure about what happened? Well, we don't know for sure what happened, but we do know that none of 知道發生什麼事？我們不確切知道經過，但肯定沒有一個 Julia, Mark and museum guide them survived. We also know that their health was affected by a number of problems. One was 人生還。我們也知道，他們的健康受多種問題影響。其中一項是 Julia, Mark and museum guide the quality of their diet. They simply didn't get enough vitamins. This is because, as I mentioned 飲食品質。他們攝取的維他命根本不足，因為如我之前所說， Julia, Mark and museum guide before, they weren't eating enough high-quality meat. OK, so not enough vitamins. What else? 沒有吃到足夠優質的肉。明白，缺乏維他命，還有呢？ Julia, Mark and museum guide They were stuck on the ice for so long, and the human body needs a huge number of calories when 他們被困冰上太久，在那樣寒冷的環境裡，人體需要大量卡路里， Julia, Mark and museum guide it's that cold. But they just didn't get enough, so they starved. They just didn't get enough 但他們攝取不足，因此餓死。他們得不到足夠的 Julia, Mark and museum guide calories to survive. Whoa, it's a grim story. Yes, it really must have been terrible. 卡路里來生存。嘩，真是悲慘的故事。是啊，情況一定很可怕。 Julia, Mark and museum guide You said they found the ship in 2010. Where? Well, it's kind of strange, actually. The name of the 你說船在 2010 年找到，是在哪裡？說來有點奇怪，那個 Julia, Mark and museum guide area was almost the same as that of the ship. It was found in an area called Shadow Bay. 地區的名字跟船名幾乎一樣，是在「暗影灣」發現的。 Julia, Mark and museum guide Oh, that's a creepy coincidence. The shadow, Shadow Bay. 這個巧合有點毛骨悚然。暗影號、暗影灣。 Julia, Mark and museum guide Another strange thing is how they found it. The story goes that a local fisherman had a dream 另一件奇怪的事，是發現它的經過。據說一名當地漁夫做了個夢， Julia, Mark and museum guide about a ship caught in a huge snowstorm on the ice. The fisherman was so upset by the dream 夢見一艘船在冰上遇上巨大暴風雪。這個夢令他非常不安， Julia, Mark and museum guide that he felt he had to go there and check for himself. And when he did, he found an old ship 覺得必須親自去看看。到達後，他找到一艘舊船， Julia, Mark and museum guide in exactly the same spot where he'd seen it in his dream. So he called the authorities, 位置跟夢裡所見一模一樣。於是他通知當局， Julia, Mark and museum guide who eventually confirmed that, yes, it was the shadow. He was right. 當局最終確認，那的確是暗影號。他說對了。 Julia, Mark and museum guide Wow, that's amazing. Imagine seeing it in a dream. 真不可思議，竟然在夢中看到它。 Narrator That is the end of task three. entries.title: The Statue of the Leopard God
entries.text: Listen to Modern Explorer, a podcast about modern-day exploration. You will hear historian Anna Connor introducing an audiobook. After you hear part of the audiobook, Anna will give her opinion on the audiobook. You do not need to answer in complete sentences. Peter Dales’ Audiobook: The Rise of the Leopard God Chapter 1: Through the Jungle Why did people think the Leopard God was more important than other gods? Why did Peter think the wild animals were not afraid of humans? Why did Peter think the guides didn’t want to continue? Chapter 2: The Statue How did Peter’s team know they had found the statue of the Leopard God? What unexpected items did Peter’s team discover at the temple? Chapter 3: The Research Why did Peter’s team take items away from the temple? Anna Connor’s opinion Why does Anna think that Peter should not say he discovered the temple? What does Anna think will happen to the other valuable items because of the audiobook? According to Anna, what is the real point of studying historical items? Narrator Task four. Listen to Modern Explorer, a podcast about modern day exploration. 任務四。請聆聽介紹現代探險的播客《Modern Explorer》。 Narrator You will hear historian Anna Connor introducing an audiobook. After you hear part of the audiobook, 你會聽到歷史學家 Anna Connor 介紹一本有聲書。聽過部分內容後， Narrator Anna will give her opinion on the audiobook. Please note that you do not need to answer in Anna 會評論這本有聲書。請注意，你不需要用 Narrator complete sentences. You now have 30 seconds to study the task. At the end of the task, 完整句子作答。你現在有三十秒閱讀題目。本任務結束後， Narrator / Modern Explorer you will have three minutes to tidy up your answers. Good morning, and welcome to the program. 你將有三分鐘整理答案。早安，歡迎收聽節目。 Modern Explorer I'm Anna Connor, and you're listening to Modern Explorer. Today, we're going to hear from an 我是 Anna Connor，你正在收聽《Modern Explorer》。今天我們會聽一位 Modern Explorer explorer called Peter Dales, who claims to have discovered a lost monument, the Temple of the 名叫 Peter Dales 的探險家分享，他聲稱發現了一處失落古蹟： Modern Explorer Leopard God. Let's hear some parts of his new audiobook, The Rise of the Leopard God. 豹神神廟。現在聽聽他的新有聲書《豹神崛起》的部分內容。 Modern Explorer Chapter one, Through the Jungle. On the first day of our search, my team and I left the jungle 第一章：穿越叢林。搜索第一天，我和團隊離開叢林 Modern Explorer campsite with two experienced guides. They knew the area well because their families had lived 營地，由兩名經驗豐富的嚮導帶路。他們很熟悉這個地方，因為家族 Modern Explorer nearby for generations, and they had grown up hearing stories of the Leopard God. Their ancestors 世世代代住在附近，而他們從小聽着豹神的故事長大。他們的祖先 Modern Explorer have the greatest respect for the Leopard God because the Leopard would have been the most 對豹神極為崇敬，因為豹應該是叢林裡最 Modern Explorer powerful animal in the jungle. Luckily, we didn't see real live leopards. We did, however, 強大的動物。幸好我們沒有見到真正活生生的豹。不過，途中確實 Modern Explorer meet some very curious wild animals on our journey. Monkeys followed us in the trees above our heads, 遇上了一些非常好奇的野生動物。猴子在我們頭上的樹梢跟着我們， Modern Explorer and small deer came out to watch us. How would they know to be scared of us if they had never 小鹿也走出來看我們。如果牠們從來沒 Modern Explorer seen humans before? This was a clear sign that people had not been in this area for a very, 見過人類，又怎會懂得害怕？這清楚顯示，人們已經很久、 Modern Explorer very long time. We continued on our journey into the valley, fighting our way through the jungle. 很久沒來過這個地方。我們繼續向山谷前進，艱難地穿過叢林。 Modern Explorer By late afternoon, though, we'd hit a problem. The guides said that they were unwilling to take 但到下午較晚時，我們遇上問題。嚮導說不願再帶我們 Modern Explorer us any further, claiming that the area was unsafe. They said that a recent earthquake 前進，聲稱該區不安全。他們說最近有一次地震， Modern Explorer had made the area dangerous, and so it was unsafe to go on. This seemed suspicious, 使這個地方變得危險，所以不能繼續走。這似乎有點可疑， Modern Explorer and it seemed to me that there may have been another reason why they didn't want to continue. 我覺得他們不願繼續，可能另有原因。 Modern Explorer The Leopard God. I actually think that they were afraid of making the Leopard God angry. 就是豹神。我其實認為他們怕惹怒豹神。 Modern Explorer According to local legend, disturbing the Leopard God could have very serious consequences. That's 根據當地傳說，打擾豹神可能帶來非常嚴重的後果。 Modern Explorer why they would not go on. We continued alone. Chapter 2. The Statue. On our second day, 所以他們不肯前進。我們獨自繼續。第二章：神像。第二天， Modern Explorer after hours of climbing through the dense jungle, we eventually reached a flat area. 在茂密叢林中攀爬了好幾個小時後，我們終於到達一片平地。 Modern Explorer Was this the site of the temple? The temple was said to have been guarded by a huge statue 這裡就是神廟所在嗎？傳說神廟由一座巨大的豹神像 Modern Explorer of the Leopard God, made entirely of blue stone. Suddenly, we made a remarkable discovery. 守護，神像完全用藍色石頭造成。忽然，我們有了驚人的發現。 Modern Explorer One colour stood out between the green leaves and brown soil. The large pieces of blue stone 在綠葉和啡色泥土之間，有一種顏色格外突出：一大塊塊藍色石頭， Modern Explorer were unmistakable. Then, all around on the ground, we began to see more and more blue stones. 絕對不會認錯。接着，我們在周圍地面看到越來越多藍石。 Modern Explorer This was it. The lost statue of the Leopard God. As we carefully removed plants and dirt, 就是這裡，失落的豹神像。我們小心清除植物和泥土時， Modern Explorer we uncovered a wonderful surprise. Under the plants was a gold coin. We began searching. 又有一個美妙驚喜：植物下面有一枚金幣。我們開始搜尋。 Modern Explorer That day alone, we uncovered more than 70 priceless gold coins, scattered all around the immediate 單是那一天，就挖出超過七十枚無價的金幣，散落在附近 Modern Explorer area. There was so much more to explore. We vowed that one day we would return. 各處。還有很多地方值得探索，我們發誓有一天會回來。 Modern Explorer Chapter 3. The Research. The next step was to take some evidence back to our research centre 第三章：研究。下一步是把一些證據帶回我們在 Modern Explorer in London. Some historians may not agree with removing artefacts, but we had two 倫敦的研究中心。部分歷史學家可能不同意把文物移走，但我們有兩個 Modern Explorer very good reasons for doing so. Firstly, we needed to study the items carefully, 很充分的理由。第一，我們需要仔細研究這些物件， Modern Explorer and the only place we could do that was in the lab. So we packed the objects up into boxes 唯一能做到這點的地方是實驗室。因此我們把物件裝箱， Modern Explorer and shipped them all back to our lab in London for analysis. The second reason 全部運回倫敦實驗室分析。第二個理由 Modern Explorer is particularly important to this discovery. There could always be an earthquake, and if that happened, 對這次發現尤其重要：這裡隨時可能再發生地震，若真的發生， Modern Explorer then the site would have been destroyed. We knew we had to take the items we found to safety, 遺址便可能被毀。我們知道必須把找到的物件帶到安全地方， Modern Explorer so that they wouldn't be lost if an earthquake struck the area again. 這樣即使地震再次襲擊，文物也不會失去。 Modern Explorer OK, so that was an extract from Peter Dale's new book, The Rise of the Leopard God. 好，以上是 Peter Dales 新書《豹神崛起》的節錄。 Modern Explorer Well, what can I say? This is all rubbish. There are so many problems here, 我能說什麼呢？全是胡說八道。問題實在太多， Modern Explorer I just don't know where to start. Firstly, and most importantly, Peter should not say he 不知從何說起。首先，也是最重要的，Peter 不應說自己 Modern Explorer discovered the temple. He didn't discover it because the local people already knew about it. 發現了神廟。他沒有發現，因為當地人早已知道它存在。 Modern Explorer The local people knew about the temple because their families had always lived in the area. 當地人知道神廟，因為他們的家族一直住在那裡。 Modern Explorer Just because someone from Europe went there to see it for themselves, 不能因為有個歐洲人親自去看過， Modern Explorer it does not mean that no one else knew about it. And for goodness sake, 就說以前沒有人知道。真是的， Modern Explorer why does he keep repeating that there is so much gold? What does he think is going to happen? 他為什麼不停強調有那麼多金子？他以為會發生什麼事？ Modern Explorer Now that we know where the temple is, anybody can go there and take the objects. 現在大家知道神廟在哪裡，任何人都可以去把物件拿走。 Modern Explorer And that would be a disaster for the local community and for historical research. 這對當地社區和歷史研究都會是災難。 Modern Explorer And Peter Dale's really needs to remember what the true value of studying historical items is. Peter Dales 真應該記住，研究歷史物件的真正價值是什麼。 Modern Explorer It is not how much they are worth. It is not what the objects are made of that's important. 不是它們值多少錢，也不是用什麼材料造的。 Modern Explorer It's how people use these things in their lives. That's what's important. 重要的是人們怎樣在生活中使用這些東西。 Modern Explorer For instance, why were there so many gold coins at the temple? 例如，神廟為什麼有那麼多金幣？ Modern Explorer What does this tell us about how people use the temple? 這讓我們了解人們怎樣使用神廟？ Modern Explorer If we find the answers to these questions, this will give us a much better picture 如果找到這些問題的答案，我們便能更清楚 Modern Explorer / Narrator of how people lived in the past. That is the end of task four and of part three A. 了解古人如何生活。任務四及卷三甲部完結。 Narrator You now have three minutes to complete your answers to task four and to tidy up 你現在有三分鐘完成任務四的答案，並整理 Narrator all your other answers. Page two of your data file. Situation. You are Nico Lin. 所有其他答案。資料檔案第二頁。情境：你是 Nico Lin。 豹神像 請聆聽介紹現代探險的播客《Modern Explorer》。歷史學家 Anna Connor 會介紹一本有聲書。播放部分內容後，她會發表意見。你毋須用完整句子作答。 Peter Dales 的有聲書：《豹神崛起》。 第一章：穿越叢林 人們為什麼認為豹神比其他神更重要？ Peter 為什麼認為野生動物不怕人？ Peter 認為嚮導不願繼續前進的原因是什麼？ 第二章：神像 Peter 的團隊怎樣知道自己找到了豹神像？ Peter 的團隊在神廟意外找到什麼物件？ 第三章：研究 Peter 的團隊為什麼把物件從神廟帶走？ Anna Connor 的意見 Anna 為什麼認為 Peter 不應說自己發現了神廟？ Anna 認為這本有聲書會令其餘珍貴物件遭遇什麼情況？ 根據 Anna，研究歷史物件的真正意義是什麼？
