Wow, no pressure there then! And where are we presenting? 所有部門主管！哇，那壓力可不小啊！我們在哪裡簡報？ Cherie The boardroom. You know, the big room on the top floor with the view and… 在董事會會議室。你知道的，就是頂樓那間很大的房間，可以看到景色，還有…… Julian Yeah, yeah, I know where the boardroom is. Well, we’d better get going then. How much do we need to get ready? I mean, how long does it have to be? 知道，知道，我知道董事會會議室在哪裡。那我們最好開始準備了。我們需要準備多少內容？我的意思是，簡報要多長？ Cherie Well, all three of us will be doing a section. So I think if we do 5 PowerPoint slides each. 嗯，我們三個人每人會負責一個部分。所以我想，如果我們每人做 5 張 PowerPoint 投影片。 Bonnie Yeah, that’s what I was thinking. 5 slides each. Which is 15 PowerPoint slides in total. 對，我也是這樣想的。每人 5 張投影片。也就是總共 15 張 PowerPoint 投影片。 Julian So, just to confirm, what were the three sections again? 所以，我再確認一下，三個部分分別是什麼？ Cherie You are joking, aren’t you? (pause) Right, I can see you’re not. Right, well Bonnie is going to look at the history of World Expos. 你是在開玩笑，對吧？（停頓）好吧，我看得出來你不是。好，Bonnie 會負責研究世界博覽會的歷史。 Julian Oh, I thought you were doing the history of World Expos! 哦，我以為是你負責世界博覽會的歷史！ Cherie No, that’s Bonnie doing that. You are looking at the good and bad things about World Expos. 不是，那是 Bonnie 負責的。你負責研究世界博覽會的好處和壞處。 Julian Yeah, yeah, I remember Jasmine did say she wanted us to find the bad things as well as the good. So, what are you doing, Cherie? 對，對，我記得 Jasmine 確實說過，她希望我們找出壞處，也要找出好處。那 Cherie，你負責什麼？ Cherie I’m looking at the future of World Expos, remember? We already read a bit on the future of World Expos online on the webpage. 我負責研究世界博覽會的未來，記得嗎？我們已經在網頁上讀過一些關於世界博覽會未來的資料。 Julian Oh, yeah, OK. I remember. 哦，對，好的。我想起來了。 Cherie Right, so what I wanted to do today was to draw up a work schedule. You know, so we know who’s doing what and when. 好，所以我今天想做的是擬定一份工作時間表。也就是讓我們知道誰負責什麼，以及什麼時候完成。 Julian OK, maybe I can take notes and send you it later. 好的，也許我可以做筆記，稍後再發給你們。 Cherie Oh, I was going to say, I was speaking to a friend of mine, Leo Roy, the other day. You know Leo? 哦，我正想說，前幾天我和我的一個朋友 Leo Roy 聊過。你認識 Leo 嗎？ Julian No, no. 不，不認識。 Bonnie Yeah, I know Leo, remember? 我認識 Leo，記得嗎？ Cherie Oh, yeah, of course (laughs). Well, Leo told me his dad worked on the Shanghai Expo in 2010, so I’ve arranged to meet up with him—his dad, I mean—and interview him. 哦，對，當然記得（笑）。Leo告訴我，他爸爸曾參與 2010 年上海世博會的工作，所以我已經安排和他見面——我是說和他爸爸見面——並訪問他。 Julian Fantastic—so when are you meeting him? 太好了——那你什麼時候和他見面？ Cherie Oh, I can’t remember. It was either the 8th or 9th of August. Something like that. 哦，我不太記得了。應該是 8 月 8 日或 9 日。差不多是那個時候。 Julian So, which was it? We’re trying to do a schedule here. 所以到底是哪一天？我們現在是在排時間表。 Cherie Right, let me check my phone. (Pause). Right, the Wednesday. 好，讓我看一下手機。（停頓）好，是星期三。 Julian Hold on. So you’re interviewing Mr. Roy on Wednesday the 9th of August. Is his surname spelled R-O-Y? 等等。所以你是在 8 月 9 日星期三訪問 Roy 先生。他的姓氏是拼作 R-O-Y 嗎？ Cherie Yes it is! 是的！ Julian You were pretty sure about that! (Laughs). 這點你倒是很肯定！（笑） Cherie Hey, did you read the email from Jasmine? She said that a Professor Leung at the Hong Kong Metropolitan University is giving a talk about World Expos. One of us should go. 嘿，你們有看 Jasmine 的電郵嗎？她說香港都會大學的 Leung教授會舉辦一場關於世界博覽會的講座。我們其中一個人應該去聽。 Bonnie Mm… Do you know when that is? 嗯……你知道是什麼時候嗎？ Cherie I think she said Saturday morning on 19th August. I can’t go to it. Bonnie, why don’t you go? You could see if we can include some of the information in our presentation on the 30th. 我想她說是 8 月 19 日星期六早上。我不能去。Bonnie，不如你去吧？你可以看看我們能否把其中一些資料放進 30 日的簡報裡。 Bonnie Yeah, great! OK, I’ll make a note of that. A talk on Expos at the Metropolitan University, on Saturday the 19th. 好啊，太好了！好的，我會記下來。19 日星期六，在都會大學有一場關於博覽會的講座。 Cherie Great. So, I think we should meet up at some point to talk about all the information we’ve collected. 很好。所以我覺得我們應該找個時間見面，討論一下我們收集到的所有資料。 Julian Good idea. When’d be a good time for you? 好主意。你什麼時候方便？ Cherie How about Monday the 21st? 21 日星期一怎麼樣？ Bonnie No, it’s a public holiday, remember? How about the day after the public holiday then? 不行，那天是公眾假期，記得嗎？那公眾假期之後一天怎麼樣？ Julian For what? Sorry, I was miles away. 做什麼？抱歉，我剛才走神了。 Cherie For the progress meeting. 開進度會議。 Julian Yeah, fine, yeah. 可以，可以。 Bonnie Yeah, me too. OK, well, then I’m happy to take all the information and do a first draft of the PowerPoint presentation if you like. 我也可以。好的，那如果你們願意，我可以把所有資料整理起來，做出 PowerPoint 簡報的初稿。 Julian Fantastic—thanks, Cherie. When do you think you can get the first draft of the PowerPoint presentation done by? Jasmine said she’d definitely have to see it beforehand. 太好了——謝謝你，Cherie。你覺得你什麼時候可以完成 PowerPoint 簡報初稿？Jasmine 說她一定要事先看過。 Cherie I can give a first draft to Jasmine on the 23rd of August. It will take me a few hours to put it all together. 我可以在 8 月 23 日把初稿交給 Jasmine。把所有內容整理起來大概會花我幾個小時。 Julian OK. Give Jasmine the first draft of the PowerPoint presentation on the 23rd of August. 好的。8 月 23 日把 PowerPoint 簡報初稿交給 Jasmine。 Cherie Great. Could we practise the presentation sometime around about then? How about doing it on Saturday 26th? All of us will need to do it. Would that be okay? 很好。那我們能不能在那前後找個時間練習簡報？8 月 26 日星期六怎麼樣？我們所有人都需要參與。可以嗎？ Bonnie Yeah, that’s fine with me. 可以，我沒問題。 Cherie Fantastic. Is that fine with you, Julian? 太好了。Julian，你也可以嗎？ Julian Sure. No problem. 當然，沒問題。 Cherie Great—looks like we are very organised. 很好——看來我們安排得很有條理。 世界博覽會簡報工作安排 Bonnie、Cherie 和 Julian 正在商討研究世界博覽會的工作時間表。請聆聽對話，完成下方筆記表。第一項已作為例子提供。 簡報詳情 簡報題目：世界博覽會概覽（例子）。 日期： 時間： 聽眾： 地點： 長度： 將涵蓋的範疇 Bonnie：世界博覽會的 。 Julian：世界博覽會的 。 Cherie：世界博覽會的 。 工作時間表 欄目：日期／負責人／工作。 ／Julian／ 8 月 19 日／Bonnie／在香港都會大學 ／全體／進度會議 8 月 23 日／ ／把 交給 Jasmine 8 月 26 日／ ／

entries.title: A history of World Expos
entries.text: You are attending a lecture by Professor Leung, who is going to talk about the history of World Expos. Listen and fill in the missing information in the space below. One has been provided as an example. Topic: A History of World Expos: Definition of World Expos: international exhibitions (example) Roles of host countries Stage 1: Industrial and Technological Inventions - Period: 1851-1938 London Expo: The Great Exhibition Number of visitors: Major achievements of this Expo: Stage 2 Stage: Period: New York Expo theme: Examples of exhibits: Number of countries which took part: Stage 3: Nation Branding Period: Hanover Expo theme: Reason why considered not to be a success: Professor Leung Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. Thank you for joining me here this evening. 各位女士、先生，晚上好。感謝大家今晚蒞臨參加。 Professor Leung In 2010, Shanghai celebrated the biggest ever World Expo. Millions of people from all over the world came to Shanghai to see the exhibits and innovations the Expo had to offer. 2010 年，上海舉辦了歷來規模最大的世界博覽會。來自世界各地的數百萬人來到上海，參觀世博會展示的展品和創新成果。 Professor Leung It is this coming together of people that makes World Expos so special to me. 正是這種人們聚集在一起的情景，使世界博覽會在我心目中特別有意義。 Professor Leung And that’s why the topic of my lecture tonight is “A History of World Expos: Bringing People Together”, because Expos do just that—they bring people together. 也正因如此，我今晚講座的題目是《世界博覽會的歷史：凝聚人群》，因為博覽會正是這樣做的——它們把人們聚集在一起。 Professor Leung So first, I thought I’d tell you a little bit about what Expos are and then we’ll explore the history of World Expos, which I shall break into three stages to show you how they developed into the World Expos we know today. 所以，首先我會先簡單介紹博覽會是什麼，然後我們會探討世界博覽會的歷史。我會把這段歷史分為三個階段，向大家說明它們是如何發展成今日我們所認識的世界博覽會。 Professor Leung What are World Expos? 什麼是世界博覽會？ Professor Leung World Expos are, quite simply, international exhibitions. 簡單來說，世界博覽會就是國際展覽。 Professor Leung One country is the host. 其中一個國家會擔任主辦國。 Professor Leung Basically, the host country has two major things to do: 基本上，主辦國有兩項主要工作： Professor Leung Decide on a theme for the exhibition. 第一，決定展覽的主題。 Professor Leung The theme is very important for the Expo as it gives it its focus. 主題對博覽會非常重要，因為它為博覽會提供焦點。 Professor Leung Having decided on a theme, the host has to invite other countries to join the exhibition. 在決定主題之後，主辦國必須邀請其他國家參與展覽。 Professor Leung History of World Expos – Three Stages 世界博覽會的歷史——三個階段 Professor Leung The first phase or stage is focused on industrial and technological inventions. 第一個階段聚焦於工業和科技發明。 Professor Leung This phase began way back in 1851 and really lasted until about 1938. 這個階段早在 1851 年開始，並一直持續到大約 1938 年。 Professor Leung So the very first World Expo was held in 1851, in the wonderful city of London, England. 第一屆世界博覽會於 1851 年在英國美麗的城市倫敦舉行。 Professor Leung It was called “The Great Exhibition”, and the idea was to promote all the very latest inventions for improving industry and farming. 它名為「萬國工業博覽會」，其理念是推廣所有能改善工業和農業的最新發明。 Professor Leung Ten countries, including China, were invited to join in and display their latest technology. 包括中國在內的十個國家受邀參與，並展示它們的最新科技。 Professor Leung 6.3 million visitors came to see the Great Exhibition. 共有 630 萬名參觀者前來參觀這場萬國工業博覽會。 Professor Leung It was a truly amazing event. 這確實是一場令人驚嘆的盛事。 Professor Leung The Great Exhibition had several major achievements, but I’d like to highlight two: 這場萬國工業博覽會有幾項重大成就，但我想重點介紹其中兩項： Professor Leung The first is what people thought was the major achievement of the Great Exhibition at the time, which was they grew the biggest flower in the world. 第一項是當時人們認為這場博覽會最重大的成就，那就是他們培育出了世界上最大的花。 Professor Leung And this flower was so big a child could stand on its leaf. 這朵花大得足以讓一個小孩站在它的葉子上。 Professor Leung The second major achievement was raising awareness of farming techniques. 第二項重大成就是提高了人們對農業技術的認識。 Professor Leung The increase of awareness of different farming techniques learnt from the Great Expo brought huge benefits to the world. 從這場博覽會學到的不同農業技術，使人們的認識提高，並為世界帶來巨大益處。 Professor Leung The second stage in the development of World Expos focused on Cultural Exchange. 世界博覽會發展的第二個階段聚焦於文化交流。 Professor Leung This stage is called “Cultural Exchange” because from about 1939 to 1987, World Expos focused more on themes that were important culturally. 這個階段稱為「文化交流」，因為從大約 1939 年到 1987 年，世界博覽會更注重具有文化意義的主題。 Professor Leung One of the first World Expos of this kind took place in New York, America, in 1939. 這類世界博覽會的早期例子之一，是 1939 年在美國紐約舉行的博覽會。 Professor Leung As I have said before, all World Expos have a particular theme, and the theme of this World Expo was “The City of Tomorrow”. 正如我之前所說，所有世界博覽會都有一個特定主題，而這屆世界博覽會的主題是「明日之城」。 Professor Leung To show the city of tomorrow, the New York Expo had huge exhibitions on modern food and displayed the latest works of art from different countries. 為了展示明日之城，紐約世博會舉辦了大型現代食品展覽，並展出來自不同國家的最新藝術作品。 Professor Leung So it combined different aspects of culture: food and art. 因此，它結合了文化的不同面向：食物和藝術。 Professor Leung Again, this was a very popular World Expo. 同樣地，這是一屆非常受歡迎的世界博覽會。 Professor Leung 50 countries took part and over 44 million people went to it. 共有 50 個國家參與，超過 4,400萬人前往參觀。 Professor Leung Finally, the third stage in the development of World Expos was really all about Nation Branding. 最後，世界博覽會發展的第三個階段主要關乎國家品牌塑造。 Professor Leung The Nation Branding stage started around 1988 and is still going on now, really. 國家品牌塑造階段大約始於 1988 年，實際上至今仍在持續。 Professor Leung This meant that the host country and all participating countries used the Expo to promote themselves. 這意味著主辦國和所有參展國都利用博覽會來宣傳自己。 Professor Leung An example of an Expo in the Nation Branding stage took place in Hanover, Germany. 國家品牌塑造階段的一個例子，是在德國漢諾威舉行的博覽會。 Professor Leung The theme for this Expo was “Nature and Technology”. 這屆博覽會的主題是「自然與科技」。 Professor Leung The idea was to promote environmentally-friendly products and inventions and to look at ways of saving the environment. 其理念是推廣環保產品和發明，並探索保護環境的方法。 Professor Leung 155 countries were invited, but unfortunately the number of visitors was lower than what had been expected. 共有 155 個國家受邀參與，但遺憾的是，參觀人數低於預期。 Professor Leung Only about 25 million people came to the Expo, so it was considered to be a bit of a failure. 只有大約 2,500 萬人前來參觀，因此它被認為有點失敗。 世界博覽會的歷史 你正在聽梁教授講解世界博覽會的歷史。請聆聽錄音，並在下方空格填上所缺資料。其中一項已作為例子提供。 講題：世界博覽會的歷史： 世界博覽會的定義：國際展覽（例子）。 主辦國的職責 第一階段：工業與科技發明——時期：1851–1938 年 倫敦世界博覽會：萬國工業博覽會。 參觀人數： 這屆博覽會的主要成就： 第二階段 階段名稱： 時期： 紐約世界博覽會的主題： 展品例子： 參展國家數目： 第三階段：國家品牌塑造 時期： 漢諾威世界博覽會的主題： 被認為不成功的原因：

entries.title: Feedback on the presentation slides
entries.text: Cherie has just shown Bonnie and Julian a draft of her PowerPoint slides for the presentation. Bonnie and Julian are now giving her some feedback. Listen to the conversation and make notes in the notesheet below. One has been provided as an example. Suggested additional PowerPoint slides - Downsides of having an Expo • • • Why countries want to hold an Expo • To promote • To build up the national image (example) • To attract Suggestions for the layout of PowerPoint slides Cherie OK, so what do you think? 好了，你們覺得怎麼樣？ Bonnie Well, I think it’s brilliant overall. You’ve done a really good job. 嗯，整體來說我覺得很出色。你做得非常好。 Cherie But… I’m sensing a “but” here! (laughs) 但是……我感覺這裡有一個「但是」！（笑） Bonnie (laughs) Well, I think it might be a bit light on content. （笑）嗯，我覺得內容可能有點不足。 Cherie OK, so I was thinking that as well. We could maybe add a couple more slides. What do you think is missing or could be expanded on? 好的，其實我也有這樣想。我們也許可以再加幾張投影片。你覺得缺少了什麼，或者有哪些地方可以再擴充？ Bonnie Yeah, I was wondering if we needed more on the downsides, you know, negatives about organising World Expos. So, I would add a slide on that. 對，我在想我們是否需要多講一些負面方面，也就是舉辦世界博覽會的壞處。所以我會加一張關於這方面的投影片。 Bonnie Maybe include some key points on the slide. The first one would be something about the millions of dollars wasted on World Expos, and the fact that the money could be better spent. 也許可以在投影片上加入一些重點。第一點可以是關於世界博覽會浪費數百萬美元，以及這些錢本可以用在更好的地方。 Julian Yeah, I’d include something like that. I mean, the host country has to be prepared to spend millions on creating a World Expo. 對，我也會加入類似的內容。我的意思是，主辦國必須準備花費數百萬美元來舉辦世界博覽會。 Julian One of the other downsides we could include is the disruption to life in the host city. 我們可以加入的另一個壞處，是對主辦城市居民生活造成的干擾。 Julian You know, World Expos have to be built and existing roads to the Expo site have to be improved or new roads have to be constructed. 你知道，世界博覽會場地必須興建，而且通往會場的現有道路必須改善，或者需要興建新道路。 Julian So, it can cause a lot of disruption for people living in the host city. 因此，這可能會對主辦城市居民的生活造成很大干擾。 Cherie Another disadvantage we could include is that very often people complain that the Expo buildings are not used again after the end of the Expo. 我們可以加入的另一個缺點是，人們經常抱怨博覽會結束後，那些博覽會建築不會再被使用。 Bonnie Really? 真的嗎？ Cherie Yeah, occasionally the buildings are re-used, but more often than not they are just taken down so, no, they’re not re-used. 是的，偶爾那些建築會被重新使用，但更多時候它們只是被拆除，所以，沒錯，它們通常不會被重用。 Cherie OK, well I think I can do a slide on that. Is there anything else to include? Another slide maybe? 好的，我覺得我可以就這一點做一張投影片。還有其他需要加入的內容嗎？也許再加一張投影片？ Bonnie Well, I think we could include one on the reasons why a city would want to host a World Expo. I don’t think that comes across in our slides. 嗯，我覺得我們可以加入一張關於為什麼一個城市會想舉辦世界博覽會的投影片。我覺得我們目前的投影片沒有清楚呈現這一點。 Cherie So, what would you include then, Bonnie? What kind of reasons? 那你會加入什麼內容呢，Bonnie？哪些理由？ Bonnie Well, there are lots of reasons. The first reason for holding a World Expo would be to promote friendship among different countries. 嗯，理由有很多。舉辦世界博覽會的第一個原因，是促進不同國家之間的友誼。 Bonnie Many different countries work together on each Expo, so it’s a wonderful way to promote international friendship. 許多不同國家會在每一屆博覽會中合作，所以這是促進國際友誼的絕佳方式。 Bonnie The second reason for holding World Expos is so that different countries that take part in World Expos can build up their national image. 舉辦世界博覽會的第二個原因，是讓參與世界博覽會的不同國家可以建立自己的國家形象。 Bonnie You know, countries can show how beautiful their countries are and how friendly their people are. 你知道，各國可以展示自己的國家有多美麗，以及人民有多友善。 Bonnie Plus, holding Expos can attract business and tourism. 此外，舉辦博覽會可以吸引商業活動和旅遊業。 Cherie Right, OK. Got it. I’ll include all these points in two extra slides. I’ll get the draft ready to give to Jasmine. Thanks guys. 好，明白了。我會把這些重點放進兩張額外的投影片裡。我會準備好初稿交給 Jasmine。謝謝你們。 Cherie Any comments on the presentation, I mean the way it looks and— 關於簡報還有什麼意見嗎？我是指它的外觀和—— Bonnie Well, I think generally it’s a bit wordy. You know too many words on each slide. 嗯，我覺得整體來說文字有點多。你知道，每張投影片上的字太多了。 Cherie So, could we take out some of the writing? 所以，我們可以刪掉一些文字嗎？ Bonnie OK, less writing, right. Hang on, let me get my laptop to write these comments down so I don’t forget. (Pause). OK. 好的，減少文字，對吧。等一下，讓我拿出筆記型電腦把這些意見記下來，免得忘記。（停頓）好了。 Julian That would help definitely. Plus I was thinking we could put in more visuals, you know, more pictures. 那肯定會有幫助。另外，我在想我們可以加入更多視覺元素，也就是更多圖片。 Julian I think it would make the presentation look much more interesting. What do you think? 我覺得這會讓簡報看起來更有趣。你覺得呢？ Cherie Sure. I can add more visuals. 當然。我可以加入更多視覺元素。 Julian Yeah, another point I thought of was to change the background colour to light blue. 對，我想到的另一點是把背景顏色改成淺藍色。 Julian White looks a bit boring, so why not have a light blue background instead of white, so it looks more colourful? 白色看起來有點沉悶，所以為什麼不用淺藍色背景取代白色，讓它看起來更有色彩？ Bonnie Yeah, I had a similar comment I’d noted down. What do you think, Cherie? 對，我也記下了類似的意見。Cherie，你覺得呢？ Cherie Yep, fine. I was actually going to do that anyway in the next draft. 可以，沒問題。其實我本來也打算在下一版初稿中這樣做。 Cherie Okay, so change the background colour to light blue. What else? 好，所以把背景顏色改成淺藍色。還有什麼？ Julian Another point is maybe put all the main headings in red instead of having all the writing in black just to make it look more interesting. 另一點是，也許可以把所有主要標題改成紅色，而不是所有文字都用黑色，這樣可以讓它看起來更有趣。 Cherie Yeah, good idea. So “put headings in red”. 對，好主意。所以是「把標題改成紅色」。 Julian Another point is the size of the writing. I think it’s a bit small—can we make it bigger so it’s easier for the audience to read? 還有一點是文字大小。我覺得字有點小——我們可以把它放大一點，讓觀眾更容易閱讀嗎？ Cherie Mmm, so “make the writing bigger”. 嗯，所以是「把文字放大」。 Julian How about changing the font too? I always think Times New Roman looks so old-fashioned. 那也改一下字體怎麼樣？我一直覺得 Times New Roman看起來很過時。 Julian Can we make it more, you know, “up-to-date” looking? 我們可以讓它看起來更，你知道，更「現代」一點嗎？ Cherie Okay, change the font to make it look more modern. 好的，改變字體，讓它看起來更現代。 Cherie Actually, in relation to that—I was wondering whether we should use numbers or bullet points. 其實，說到這一點，我在想我們應該使用編號還是項目符號。 Cherie In the end, I used numbers, but do you think bullet points would look better? 最後我用了編號，但你們覺得項目符號會不會看起來更好？ Bonnie Yeah I do—less formal and more visual— 對，我覺得會——比較不正式，也更有視覺效果—— Cherie Okay, so change numbers to bullet points. Right, OK. Got it. I’ll get the draft ready to give to Jasmine then. Thanks guys. 好的，所以把編號改成項目符號。好，明白了。那我會準備好初稿交給 Jasmine。謝謝你們。 簡報投影片的意見 Cherie 剛向 Bonnie 和 Julian 展示了她製作的 PowerPoint 投影片初稿。Bonnie 和 Julian 現在正向她提供意見。請聆聽對話，並在下方筆記表記下資料。其中一項已作為例子提供。 建議新增的 PowerPoint 投影片：舉辦世界博覽會的弊端 各國希望舉辦世界博覽會的原因 推動 。 建立國家形象（例子）。 吸引 。 PowerPoint 投影片版面設計建議

entries.title: Ota Benga and the darker history of World Expos
entries.text: Julian, Bonnie and Cherie have met up with their friend Leo at a cafe. They are talking about the group's presentation and World Expos. Listen to the conversation and answer the questions below. You do not need to answer in complete sentences. One has been provided as an example. Ota Benga Ota Benga What, according to Leo, was the main function of World Expos for ordinary people? How many people were exhibited in human zoos in World Expos at the end of the 19th Century and the beginning of the 20th Century? Name three activities that people exhibited in human zoos had to do lived in traditional houses (example) Why were Ota Benga and his tribespeople chosen by W. J. McGee for the St. Louis Expo of 1904? For what purpose did the pygmies think they were in the USA, and how did it contrast with the Expo's publicity? The pygmies thought but actually What was Ota Benga's job in the zoo in New York? How did the people of New York react? Did Ota Benga's story have a happy ending? Why / Why not? Should Ota Benga's story be included in the presentation? Give each person's reason Bonnie: Cherie: Julian: Leo OK, right, I’ve got my cappuccino. Anybody else want anything? 好了，我拿到我的卡布奇諾了。還有誰想要什麼嗎？ Bonnie No thanks. 不用了，謝謝。 Cherie No, no. 不用，不用。 Julian No, thanks Leo. How you doing anyway? 不用了，謝謝 Leo。你最近怎麼樣？ Leo I’m OK. 我還好。 Julian Good. 那就好。 Leo Right, well, I remembered you said to look out for some stuff about Expos, so I asked my dad and he sent me a link on YouTube. 好，嗯，我記得你們說過要我留意一些關於博覽會的資料，所以我問了我爸爸，他傳給我一個 YouTube 連結。 Leo I thought it might be quite interesting for you. 我覺得這對你們來說可能挺有意思。 Leo You did say you were looking into the negative aspects of World Expos and trade fairs, so this you might call the dark side of the history. 你們確實說過正在研究世界博覽會和商展的負面方面，所以這可以說是歷史中黑暗的一面。 Cherie Really? 真的嗎？ Leo Yeah, the clip was basically about the experiences of this one African man called Ota Benga. 是的，那段影片主要是關於一名叫 Ota Benga 的非洲男子的經歷。 Leo The clip started off giving a pretty interesting insight into these World Exhibitions. 影片一開始對這些世界展覽提出了一個相當有趣的觀點。 Leo They said the main function of these expos for ordinary people wasn’t trade or science but rather it was the only way that normal people could see things from around the world. 影片說，這些博覽會對普通人而言，主要功能並不是貿易或科學，而是普通人能看到世界各地事物的唯一方式。 Leo Very few people could travel abroad in those days, of course. 當然，在那個年代，能出國旅行的人非常少。 Julian Yeah, I’d never thought of that. 對，我從來沒有那樣想過。 Leo Yeah, so that was one thing. 是的，這是一方面。 Leo But there was also this other more sinister, darker side of the Expos and fairs where they exhibited humans from different parts of the world, like in a human zoo. 但博覽會和商展還有另一個更陰暗、更可怕的一面，就是它們會展示來自世界不同地方的人，就像人類動物園一樣。 Leo They reckon that more than 35,000 men, women and children were exhibited in these types of human zoos at various Expos in Paris, London, the USA… at the end of the 19th and into the 20th Century. 據估計，在 19 世紀末到 20 世紀初，超過 35,000 名男女和兒童曾在巴黎、倫敦、美國等地各種博覽會中的這類人類動物園裡被展出。 Bonnie Really? What did they make these people do in these human zoos? 真的嗎？他們讓這些人在那些人類動物園裡做什麼？ Leo Well, once there, they had to live in traditional houses. 嗯，他們到那裡之後，必須住在傳統房屋裡。 Leo These traditional houses were built especially there. 這些傳統房屋是特地在那裡建造的。 Leo And these people, they did the cooking and so on. 而這些人會做飯等等。 Leo And people watched them like they watch monkeys at a zoo. 人們觀看他們，就像在動物園裡看猴子一樣。 Leo And at certain times of the day, they put on some sort of exotic show—doing some dances or religious rituals, that sort of thing. 在一天中的某些時段，他們還要表演某種異國風情的節目——例如跳舞或進行宗教儀式之類的活動。 Julian Wow, so it was really like the dolphin show at Ocean Park, then. 哇，那真的就像海洋公園的海豚表演一樣。 Leo Yeah, pretty much. 對，差不多就是那樣。 Leo The most famous of these people who was in one of these human zoos was an African man named Ota Benga. 在這些人類動物園中，最有名的人之一是一名叫 Ota Benga的非洲男子。 Leo He was a pygmy. 他是俾格米人。 Bonnie A what? 什麼人？ Leo A pygmy, you know, a tribe from Western Africa who were smaller than average humans. 俾格米人，你知道的，就是來自西非的一個部族，他們的身形比一般人矮小。 Cherie Oh yeah, right. 哦，對，明白了。 Leo And that was the point. That’s why he was there. 而這正是重點。那就是他被帶到那裡的原因。 Julian What? Because he was a pygmy? 什麼？因為他是俾格米人？ Leo Yeah. You see, for the 1904 Great World Fair in St Louis in the USA, there was this American scientist called W.J. McGee. 對。你看，在 1904 年美國聖路易舉行的世界博覽會上，有一位名叫 W.J. McGee 的美國科學家。 Leo Now, McGee wanted to put on a spectacular exhibition of humankind. McGee 想舉辦一場壯觀的人類展覽。 Leo He wanted to exhibit the most extreme examples of man from around the world: the tallest, the smallest. That sort of thing. 他想展出來自世界各地最極端的人類例子：最高的人、最矮的人，諸如此類。 Leo So he got the smallest people from Africa. 所以他找來了非洲最矮小的人。 Leo And that was Ota Benga. 那就是 Ota Benga。 Leo He was from the tribe of pygmies—the smallest people in the world. 他來自俾格米部族——被視為世界上最矮小的人群。 Leo So, McGee sent this explorer on a huge expedition to Africa to find pygmies and bring them back. 因此，McGee 派了一名探險家前往非洲進行大規模遠征，尋找俾格米人並把他們帶回來。 Leo So, he did. He brought back Ota Benga and five other pygmies. 於是，那名探險家照做了。他帶回了 Ota Benga 和另外五名俾格米人。 Bonnie Wow. 哇。 Julian That’s amazing. 真令人驚訝。 Leo Yeah, I know. 對，我知道。 Leo The irony was that Ota Benga and his fellow tribespeople thought that they were in the USA to show off their own culture, whereas, in fact, what they were advertised to the public and scientists as was the most primitive people on the planet. 諷刺的是，Ota Benga 和他的族人以為他們到美國是為了展示自己的文化；然而事實上，他們被宣傳給公眾和科學家的形象，卻是地球上最原始的人。 Cherie That’s terrible. 這太可怕了。 Julian And what happened after the fair ended? 那博覽會結束後發生了什麼？ Leo Well, after the end of the fair, Ota went to New York. 嗯，博覽會結束後，Ota去了紐約。 Leo You imagine this little African guy in New York? You know, with all its skyscrapers and hi-tech lifestyle. 你能想像這個身材矮小的非洲男子在紐約嗎？你知道，那裡有那麼多摩天大樓和高科技生活方式。 Julian So, what did he do in New York? Did he work or? 那他在紐約做什麼？他有工作嗎，還是？ Leo Well, sort of. He then became famous because he got a job at a zoo in New York. 嗯，算是有吧。後來他因為在紐約一家動物園找到一份工作而變得有名。 Leo He thought he was going to look after the elephants, but he was actually given a job to be a live exhibit in the zoo. 他以為自己會去照顧大象，但事實上，他得到的工作是在動物園裡當一個活體展品。 Leo He shared a cage with a chimpanzee. 他和一隻黑猩猩共用一個籠子。 Bonnie That’s awful. 這太糟糕了。 Leo Well, to be fair to people in New York, they did protest and write to the newspapers complaining about it. 嗯，公平地說，紐約人確實有抗議，也有寫信給報紙投訴這件事。 Julian So, what happened? 那後來怎樣？ Leo The exhibition was stopped after about a week. 那個展覽大約一週後就被停止了。 Bonnie Good. So, then what happened to him? 太好了。那他之後怎樣？ Leo Well, it just got worse and worse for Ota. 嗯，對 Ota 來說，情況只是變得越來越糟。 Leo He then tried to settle in America and even ended up working in a tobacco factory, in a small town in the US. 後來他嘗試在美國定居，甚至最後在美國一個小鎮的煙草工廠工作。 Leo But he was so homesick that he wanted to return to Africa but he didn’t have enough money to pay for the journey, so in the end he never returned to Africa. 但他非常思鄉，想回到非洲，卻沒有足夠的錢支付旅費，所以最後他再也沒有回到非洲。 Julian That’s terrible. No wonder it’s not very well known. 這太可悲了。難怪這件事不太為人所知。 Bonnie That is a truly horrendous story, Leo. Leo，這真是一個極其可怕的故事。 Cherie God, how can you treat somebody like that? 天啊，怎麼可以那樣對待一個人？ Leo So, are you going to include it in the presentation? 那你們會把這件事放進簡報裡嗎？ Julian What do you think, Bonnie? Bonnie，你覺得呢？ Bonnie I think we should. Jasmine wanted the full picture, so this gives them the full picture of the history of these types of Expos, that’s for sure. 我覺得應該放。Jasmine 想要完整的圖像，而這肯定能讓他們更全面了解這類博覽會的歷史。 Julian Mm. Cherie? 嗯。Cherie 呢？ Cherie Well, I’m not so keen. I mean, you have to remember that a couple of the audience when we present are actually American, from the USA. 嗯，我不是很贊成。我的意思是，你們要記得，我們簡報時有幾位觀眾其實是美國人，來自美國。 Cherie I mean, we don’t want to offend anybody with our presentation, do we? What do you think, Julian? 我的意思是，我們不想因為簡報而冒犯任何人，對吧？Julian，你覺得呢？ Julian Well, I think we should. But only the first half of his story is directly relevant to expos. 嗯，我覺得應該放。不過，他故事的前半部分才和博覽會有直接關係。 Julian His experiences in New York and the zoo are less relevant. 他在紐約和動物園的經歷就沒有那麼相關。 Julian So, just including the first half would keep it relevant. 所以，只放前半部分可以讓內容保持相關。 Ota Benga 與世界博覽會的陰暗歷史 Julian、Bonnie 和 Cherie 在咖啡店與朋友 Leo 見面。他們正在談論小組的簡報與世界博覽會。請聆聽對話，回答下列問題。你不需要用完整句子作答。其中一項已作為例子提供。 Ota Benga（奧塔・本加） 根據 Leo 的說法，世界博覽會對一般大眾的主要作用是什麼？ 十九世紀末至二十世紀初，有多少人在世界博覽會的人類動物園中被展示？ 列出被展示的人必須進行的三項活動。 住在傳統房屋裡（例子）。 W. J. McGee 為什麼選中 Ota Benga 和他的族人，讓他們參加 1904 年聖路易斯世界博覽會？ 這些俾格米人以為自己到美國有什麼目的？這與博覽會的宣傳有什麼不同？ 他們以為 ，但實際上 。 Ota Benga 在紐約動物園的工作是什麼？ 紐約市民有什麼反應？ Ota Benga 的故事有美滿結局嗎？為什麼有／沒有？ 簡報應否加入 Ota Benga 的故事？請寫出每個人的理由。 Bonnie： Cherie： Julian：

entries.title: An extraordinary career and life story
entries.text: Candice and Monica are interviewing their first guest about her life story and career. Listen and write the information in the spaces below. The first one has been provided as an example. What is the name of the show? Extraordinary Hong Kong People (example) Who is their guest? Which year did she move to Hong Kong? Which part of Hong Kong did her family move to? What was her father's job? Air Traffic Controller Rescue Plane Navigator Airport Security Officer Jet Pilot Instructor What type of aircraft does she fly? Why did she choose to fly that kind of aircraft? (Give TWO reasons) Story of how she met her husband He was a of a cargo ship. One day, when he was sailing in the Lamma Channel, he broke his when he . She then flew him to . What kind of club did they meet at one year later? Where did she ask him out for a date? Exam Narrator Task 1. Candice and Monica are interviewing their first guest about her life story and career. Listen and write the information in the spaces below. The first one has been provided as an example. You now have 30 seconds to study the task. At the end of the task, 任務一。Candice 和 Monica 正在訪問首位嘉賓，了解她的人生經歷和職業生涯。請聆聽錄音，並在下方空格填寫資料。第一項已作為例子提供。你現在有三十秒時間閱讀題目。本任務結束後， Exam Narrator you will have one minute to tidy up your answers. 你將有一分鐘時間整理答案。 Candice／Monica Hello there, everyone in Cyberland. This is Candice. And this is Monica. And we are Extraordinary Hong Kong People. 網絡世界的各位，你們好！我是 Candice。我是 Monica。我們是《非凡香港人》（Extraordinary Hong Kong People）。 Candice and Monica And our extraordinary guest today is, drum roll please, our extraordinary mother. 今天這位非凡的嘉賓就是——請來點鼓聲——我們非凡的媽媽！ Candice / Monica / Mother Hello mum. Mum. Oh my, you two are really putting on a show. Hello to all your viewers. 主持人：媽媽，你好！媽媽！ 媽媽：哎呀，你們兩個真會搞氣氛。各位觀眾，你們好。 Candice／Monica Now mum, you have had an extraordinary career but before we get to that let's find out about your life. First of all, when did you come to Hong Kong? 媽媽，你的職業生涯很不平凡。不過，談工作之前，我們先了解一下你的人生經歷。首先，你是什麼時候來香港的？ Mother I was born in Guangzhou but I'm not saying when and we moved to Hong Kong. 我在廣州出生，不過我可不會說是哪一年。後來我們搬來香港。 Candice / Monica / Mother When was that again? It was three years before they started work on Chek Lap Kok Airport. 讓我想想，那是什麼時候來着？是在赤鱲角機場動工前三年。 Candice／Monica Didn't they begin building the airport in 1991? So three years before then? 機場不是在 1991 年開始興建嗎？所以是在那之前三年？ Mother Yes, 1988. That was a long time ago. I was a young girl. My father, your Grandpa Choi, 對，1988 年。那是很久以前的事了，當時我還是個小女孩。我爸爸，也就是你們的 Choi 外公， Candice / Monica / Mother moved us to East Point in Hong Kong. East Point? So Grandpa Choi has always lived in East Point? That's a long time. I remember him giving us tours of the air traffic control tower when we were little. It was so exciting. That's what I thought too when I was a girl and that's when I fell in love with flying. And yet you did not follow in Grandpa's footsteps and become an air traffic controller. No, I wanted to fly but I wasn't interested in planes or jets or airliners or anything like that. As far back as I can remember, I always wanted to be a helicopter pilot. 媽媽：把我們一家搬到香港的東角。 主持人：東角？所以 Choi 外公一直住在東角？那真的很久了。我記得小時候，他帶我們參觀航空交通管制塔，真令人興奮。 媽媽：我小時候也有同樣感受，就是那時開始愛上飛行。 主持人：可是你沒有跟隨外公的職業道路，成為航空交通管制員。 媽媽：沒有。我想親自飛行，但對飛機、噴射機、客機之類都不感興趣。從我有記憶以來，我就一直想當直升機機師。 Candice / Monica / Mother But why did you want to be a helicopter pilot specifically? What's the appeal? The appeal? 主持人：但為什麼偏偏想當直升機機師？它有什麼吸引力？ 媽媽：吸引力？ Mother Well, gosh, let me see now. First of all, I love the noise helicopters make. It's so powerful. 嗯，讓我想想。首先，我很喜歡直升機發出的聲音，那聲音很有力量。 Candice / Monica / Mother Oh mom, really? The noise? You betcha. So what's the other thing? Well, 主持人：真的嗎，媽媽？你喜歡的是聲音？ 媽媽：當然啦。 主持人：那另一點呢？ 媽媽：嗯， Mother the other thing is being able to land anywhere. I still think it's amazing. 另一點就是能夠在任何地方降落。我至今仍覺得這很神奇。 Candice / Monica / Mother Anywhere you need to land, you can. But you're not just a regular helicopter pilot, you're a rescue helicopter pilot. Which brings us to your extraordinary story. Candice? How you and Dad met is very, very romantic. Please share this story with our followers. 媽媽：需要在哪裡降落，就能在哪裡降落。 主持人：不過，你不只是一般的直升機機師，而是救援直升機機師。這就帶到你那段非凡的故事了。Candice？你和爸爸相識的經過很浪漫，請跟我們的追蹤者分享一下。 Mother Well, I rescued your father in my helicopter. He was the captain on one of those huge cargo ships. He was sailing a ship in the Lamma Channel when he broke his ankle. 我當時駕駛直升機救了你們的爸爸。他是其中一艘大型貨船的船長，當時正駕船航經南丫海峽，卻弄斷了腳踝。 Candice／Monica Oh poor dad. How did he break his ankle? Was it in a terrible storm? Did the ship sink? 可憐的爸爸！他怎樣弄斷腳踝的？遇上了猛烈風暴嗎？船沉了嗎？ Mother Oh, stop it you two. You know perfectly well what happened. He fell down some stairs on the ship. 你們兩個別鬧了。明明知道發生了什麼事。他是在船上跌下了幾級樓梯。 Candice／Monica Poor dad. It's so undramatic falling down the stairs. 可憐的爸爸。原來只是跌下樓梯，一點也不驚險。 Mother Yes, but if you fell down some stairs and broke your ankle, you wouldn't be laughing. 是啊，不過如果換了是你跌下樓梯，還弄斷了腳踝，你就笑不出來了。 Candice／Monica So what happened after that? So did you meet him then? When you were flying him to the hospital? 那之後怎樣？你就是在駕直升機送他去醫院時認識他的嗎？ Mother Of course not. I only saw him then, but I didn't speak to him. I was flying the helicopter. Besides, that would be completely unprofessional. 當然不是。我當時只是見到他，沒有跟他說話，因為我正在駕駛直升機。而且，那樣做完全不專業。 Candice／Monica I know, I know. You are very professional, Mum. 知道啦，知道啦。媽媽，你很專業。 Mother Thank you for noticing. So actually, it was about a year after I rescued him when I first spoke to him. You see, I joined a rock climbing club. Your father and I were in the same group of beginners. 謝謝你留意到。其實，我是在救他約一年後才第一次跟他交談。那時我加入了一個攀岩會，你爸爸和我都在同一個初學者小組。 Candice／Monica So what happened? Did you rescue him again at the rock climbing club? 那後來怎樣？你又在攀岩會救了他一次嗎？ Mother No, we were both good at rock climbing. What actually happened was when I told him I flew rescue helicopters. He told me about his accident, and we quickly put two and two together. 不是，我們兩個攀岩都很拿手。實際情況是，我告訴他自己駕駛救援直升機，他就提到自己的意外。我們很快便把兩件事連起來，明白原來之前已經見過。 Candice／Monica And we were the result. 而我們就是這段姻緣的成果。 Mother More was the pity. Anyway, it wasn't love at first sight. He was so shy back then. It was a few months after joining the rock climbing club that I asked him out on a date. 那可真是太可惜了。總之，那並不是一見鍾情。他那時很害羞。加入攀岩會幾個月後，是我主動邀請他約會的。 Candice／Monica Then it was love. 然後就墮入愛河了。 Mother It was so funny because I asked him out when we were on top of a cliff. I'm not sure if he looked nervous because I asked him out, or because we were on top of a cliff. But he said yes. 有趣的是，我是在我們站在懸崖頂時邀請他的。我也不確定他看起來緊張，是因為我邀請他約會，還是因為我們當時在懸崖頂。不過，他答應了。 Exam Narrator That is the end of task one. 任務一完結。 非凡的職業生涯與人生故事 Candice 和 Monica 正在訪問首位嘉賓，了解她的人生經歷和職業生涯。請聆聽錄音，並在下方空格填寫資料。第一項已作為例子提供。 節目叫什麼名字？《非凡香港人》（Extraordinary Hong Kong People）（例子） 她們的嘉賓是誰？ 她在哪一年搬到香港？ 她一家搬到香港哪個地區？ 她父親從事什麼工作？ A 航空交通管制員 B 救援飛機領航員 C 機場保安人員 D 噴射機飛行教練 她駕駛哪一類飛行器？ 她為什麼選擇駕駛那一類飛行器？（提供兩個原因） 她與丈夫相識的經過 他是一艘貨船的 。有一天，他駕船航經南丫海峽時，因為 而弄斷了 。 她隨後駕直升機把他送往 。 一年後，他們在什麼類型的社團再次相遇？ 她在哪裡邀請他約會？

entries.title: Marble racing and the Marble Olympics
entries.text: Candice is chatting to Ranbir Singh about marble racing, a pastime gaining popularity in Hong Kong. Listen and fill in the missing information in the spaces below. One has been provided as an example. Teams line up for a marble racing event Teams line up for a marble racing event Marbles are little glass balls that children play with (example) History of Lars Jensen 2011 Started building marble race tracks , which became crowded. 2013 Started of marble racing. The races were but . 2016 Began the Marble Olympics and invited to join. Marble Olympic events Relay Race Relay race human version The marble hits a and the of the marble pushes the next marble forward. High Jump High jump human version The marble rolls down a to build up enough speed to fly over a . Outdoor Marathon Outdoor marathon human version The track is made of with carefully placed . Marbles and the future Ranbir's plan for next year is to to the Tokyo Marble Olympics. In the future, Ranbir thinks marble technology will . Exam Narrator Task two. Candice is chatting to Ranbir Singh about marble racing. A pastime gaining popularity in Hong Kong. Listen and fill in the missing information in the spaces below. One has been provided as an example. You now have 30 seconds to study the task. 任務二。Candice 正在與 Ranbir Singh 談論彈珠競賽，這項消閒活動在香港日漸流行。請聆聽錄音，並在下方空格填上所缺資料。其中一項已作為例子提供。你現在有三十秒時間閱讀題目。 Exam Narrator At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers. 本任務結束後，你將有一分鐘時間整理答案。 Candice OK, everyone. Today we have Ranbir Singh, whose marble racing competitions on YouTube have become an internet sensation in Hong Kong with millions of views. Welcome, Ranbir. So why don't we start with what's what? What's the history? What's this all about? 各位，今天我們請來 Ranbir Singh。他在 YouTube 上的彈珠競賽影片在香港引起熱潮，觀看次數達數百萬。歡迎你，Ranbir。不如先由基本的介紹開始吧：它有什麼歷史？這究竟是怎樣的一回事？ Ranbir Singh Thank you, Candice. So, I'm sure you viewers know what marbles are. Those little glass balls that children play with. Well, what your viewers may not know is that you can race marbles. Not only that, you can do all sorts of competitions. And that's what I've been doing for the last four years. But the story of marble racing actually begins more than 10 years ago, with someone called Lars Jensen, who's from the Netherlands. 謝謝你，Candice。我想觀眾都知道彈珠是什麼，就是小朋友玩的那些小玻璃球。不過，大家未必知道彈珠也可以競速。不止如此，還可以進行各式各樣的比賽，而這就是我過去四年一直在做的事。不過，彈珠競賽的故事其實始於十多年前，主角是來自荷蘭的 Lars Jensen。 Ranbir Singh Back in 2011, Lars started racing marbles by making all of these different marble race tracks. These race tracks were amazing, and he made all the tracks in his bedroom at home. After watching this, I'd recommend that you click on the links below, and you'll see a video of Lars in his bedroom in 2011 with all of the tracks. 早在 2011 年，Lars 就開始製作各種彈珠賽道，讓彈珠競速。那些賽道很精彩，而且全都建在他家中的睡房裡。看完這段影片後，我建議大家點擊下方連結，看看他在 2011 年身處睡房、四周都是賽道的影片。 Candice That's pretty crowded. 那可真夠擠迫的。 Ranbir Singh Then, in 2013, Lars started making YouTube videos of marble racing. Those were really the first marble racing videos ever. Back in 2013, the races were very simple compared to the races we see on his YouTube channel nowadays. Very simple, but still fun to watch. In 2016, Lars founded the Marble Olympics. 到了 2013 年，Lars 開始製作彈珠競賽的 YouTube 影片。那確實是最早的彈珠競賽影片。跟如今在他頻道上看到的比賽相比，2013 年的比賽很簡單。雖然簡單，但看起來仍然很有趣。2016 年，Lars 創辦了彈珠奧運會。 Ranbir Singh So, to start the Olympics, he invited teams from 15 other countries to the Marble Olympics to take part in different events. So now he holds the Olympics every two years in a different city, and teams from other countries go to compete. 為了開辦這個奧運會，他邀請了另外十五個國家的隊伍參加不同項目。現在他每兩年在不同城市舉辦一次奧運會，其他國家的隊伍也會前來競賽。 Candice Can you tell us more about some of those events? 你可以再介紹其中一些項目嗎？ Ranbir Singh Okay, so let's have a closer look at some of the main Olympic events. Now, if your viewers haven't seen these, you have to remember that the marbles take the place of humans. So, for instance, one of the most popular events is the relay race. Now, in a regular human relay race, one runner passes a baton to another runner. But in the Marble Olympics, imagine there are two marbles who are the runners. 好，我們來仔細看看幾項主要的奧運項目。如果觀眾還沒看過，請記住，彈珠在比賽中代替了人。例如，最受歡迎的項目之一是接力賽。在一般的真人接力賽中，一名跑手把接力棒交給另一名跑手。換成彈珠奧運會，就想像兩顆彈珠是那兩名跑手。 Ranbir Singh The first marble rolls down a track until it hits a gate. That gate stops the first marble, but the force of the marble knocks the second marble forward, and the second marble now rolls. So it's the force of that first marble that's the important thing. Right, let's see. Another example. The high jump. As with the human high jump, a pole is placed at different heights. 第一顆彈珠沿賽道滾下，直到撞上一道擋閘。擋閘會擋停第一顆彈珠，但它撞擊產生的力會把第二顆彈珠推前，令第二顆開始滾動。所以，關鍵是第一顆彈珠的撞擊力。再看看另一個例子：跳高。跟真人跳高一樣，橫桿會放在不同高度。 Ranbir Singh But instead of using leg power, marbles don't have legs, of course, the marble gets its jumping power from rolling down a slope. So the marble goes down the slope faster and faster and uses its speed. I mean, the speed it gets from going down the slope, to fly up and over the pole. So that's the high jump. 不過，彈珠當然沒有腳，不能用腿部力量起跳。它的跳躍動力來自沿斜坡往下滾動。彈珠越滾越快，利用下坡時累積的速度飛起，越過橫桿。這就是彈珠跳高。 Ranbir Singh My favourite of all the events is the outdoor marathon. So, an outdoor marathon for humans will have runners race through forests and mountains. In the marble version, the marbles roll down a course that has been cut into sand, usually on a beach. So the course is cut into sand, but there are obstacles like sticks and stones put at various places on the course. 我最喜歡的項目是戶外馬拉松。真人的戶外馬拉松會讓跑手穿越森林和山地。彈珠版本則讓彈珠沿着在沙地挖出的路線滾下，通常是在沙灘上。路線在沙地挖成，途中不同位置還會放置樹枝、石頭等障礙物。 Ranbir Singh What I really love is when the marbles get stuck behind one of the obstacles. That's what makes it great viewing. It's brilliant to watch. 我最喜歡看到彈珠被卡在障礙物後面。這正是比賽好看的地方，看起來非常精彩。 Candice So, what's the future for marble racing? 那彈珠競賽的未來會怎樣？ Ranbir Singh Well, marble racing has become really popular across the world, especially during the pandemic. Next year, the Marble Olympics will be held for the first time in five years, and they'll be held in Tokyo, and I plan to take a Hong Kong team there. It'll be a historical moment for marble racing in Hong Kong. And beyond that, with all these international teams joining the Olympics, 彈珠競賽在世界各地都變得很受歡迎，尤其是在疫情期間。明年彈珠奧運會將是五年來首次舉行，地點是東京。我計劃帶一支香港隊前往，這將是香港彈珠競賽的歷史時刻。再往後看，隨着這麼多國際隊伍參加奧運會， Ranbir Singh I'm sure you're going to see advances in marble technology. Countries will want their marbles to win, and I predict that marble technology will become much more advanced. 我相信彈珠技術一定會進步。各國都希望自己的彈珠獲勝，所以我預測彈珠技術會變得先進得多。 Candice I used to worry about advanced robots taking over the world. Now I'm worried it will be the marbles instead. 我以前擔心先進的機械人會接管世界，現在反而擔心接管世界的會是彈珠了。 Exam Narrator That is the end of task two. 任務二完結。 彈珠競賽與彈珠奧運會 Candice 正在與 Ranbir Singh 談論彈珠競賽，這項消閒活動在香港日漸流行。請聆聽錄音，並在下方空格填上所缺資料。其中一項已作為例子提供。 各隊在彈珠競賽開始前列隊。 彈珠是：小朋友玩的小玻璃球。（例子） Lars Jensen 的發展歷程 2011 年：開始在 建造彈珠賽道，令那裡變得擠迫。 2013 年：開始 ，內容是彈珠競賽。 比賽雖然 ，但 。 2016 年：創辦彈珠奧運會，並邀請 參加。 彈珠奧運會的比賽項目 表格欄目：比賽項目／真人版本／彈珠版本。 接力賽：圖中為真人接力賽。彈珠撞上一道 ，彈珠的 把下一顆彈珠推前。 跳高：圖中為真人跳高。彈珠沿 往下滾，累積足夠速度，飛越 。 戶外馬拉松：圖中為真人戶外馬拉松。賽道由 造成，並在適當位置放置 。 彈珠競賽的未來 Ranbir 明年的計劃是 前往東京彈珠奧運會。 Ranbir 認為，未來彈珠技術會 。

entries.title: Mr Suess, the Internet cat influencer
entries.text: Monica is hosting a discussion on a cat called Mr Suess, who has become a popular Internet influencer. With Monica are Estella Webber, owner of the cat, and Max Hui, chair of the Hong Kong Cat Shelter. Listen to the conversation and make notes in the notesheet below. You do not need to answer in complete sentences. Mr Suess Mr Suess Facts about Mr Suess Has followers. Is more influential than according to . Things Mr Suess is famous for Methods used by Estella to train her cat Places the food treat where she . Repeats the action but , because . Reasons why cat videos are more popular than dog videos on YouTube Benefits of Internet cat influencers Concern about Internet cat influencers Exam Narrator Task three. Monica is hosting a discussion on a cat called Mr Suess, who has become a popular internet influencer. With Monica are Estella Webber, owner of the cat, and Max Hui, chair of the Hong Kong Cat Shelter. Listen to the conversation and make notes in the note sheet below. 任務三。Monica 正在主持一場討論，主角是已成為知名網紅的貓 Mr Suess。與她一起參與討論的有貓主人 Estella Webber，以及香港貓咪收容所主席 Max Hui。請聆聽對話，並在下方筆記表記下資料。 Exam Narrator Please note that you do not need to answer in complete sentences. You now have 30 seconds to study the task. At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers. 請注意，你不需要用完整句子作答。你現在有三十秒時間閱讀題目。本任務結束後，你將有一分鐘時間整理答案。 Monica Welcome Estella and internet sensation, Mr Suess. 歡迎 Estella，還有網絡紅星 Mr Suess。 Estella Webber Say hello, Mr Suess. Look, he's smiling. What's that, Mr Suess? He says he loves your show. Mr Suess，打個招呼吧。看，牠在笑。你說什麼，Mr Suess？牠說牠很喜歡你的節目。 Monica Thank you, Mr Suess. And welcome, Max, from the Hong Kong Cat Shelter. 謝謝你，Mr Suess。也歡迎來自香港貓咪收容所的 Max。 Max Hui Nice to meet you, Monica, Estella, Mr Suess. 很高興認識你們，Monica、Estella，還有 Mr Suess。 Monica Now, I have to say, I don't think we've ever had as big a star as Mr Suess on our show. So this is a great honor. Just in case you don't know Mr Suess, Mr Suess has 4.1 million followers on YouTube. 我得說，我們節目大概從沒請過像 Mr Suess 這麼大牌的明星，真是十分榮幸。萬一大家還不認識牠：Mr Suess 在 YouTube 上有四百一十萬名追蹤者。 Estella Webber 4.12 million as of yesterday, actually. 其實，截至昨天是四百一十二萬。 Monica I stand corrected. Sorry, Mr Suess. Getting even more popular by the day. And he is considered more influential than the TV news, according to a recent survey. 我接受更正。不好意思，Mr Suess，牠真是一天比一天受歡迎。而且，根據最近一項調查，牠被認為比電視新聞更有影響力。 Estella Webber That's right. More people watch Mr Suess than they watch the TV news every day. That survey was very recent too, only a few days ago. 沒錯，每天看 Mr Suess 的人比看電視新聞的人還多。那項調查也很新，只是幾天前的事。 Monica Then I guess the big question is why. I mean, he's cute, but how come he's such a huge success? 那最大的問題大概就是為什麼了。牠是很可愛，但為什麼會這麼成功？ Estella Webber Well, Mr Suess is famous for three things. First is that Mr Suess simply loves dressing up as superheroes. He's dressed up as Batman, Superman, Iron Man, all the superheroes. Mr Suess 因三件事出名。首先，牠很喜歡扮成超級英雄。牠扮過蝙蝠俠、超人、鐵甲奇俠，各種超級英雄都扮過。 Max Hui I'm not sure Mr Suess loves dressing up as superheroes. 我可不肯定 Mr Suess 真喜歡扮成超級英雄。 Estella Webber Yes, he does, actually. 牠真的喜歡。 Max Hui And I suppose he dances too. 我想，牠還會跳舞吧。 Estella Webber Don't be silly. As if Mr Suess would dance. He's far more talented than that. Mr Suess plays the piano. In fact, his piano playing videos are the most popular ones. And the other thing that makes him an internet sensation is that Mr Suess gets gifts from all over the world. 別說傻話了，Mr Suess 才不會跳舞。牠的才華遠不止於此：牠會彈鋼琴。事實上，牠彈琴的影片最受歡迎。另外一件令牠成為網絡紅星的事，就是牠收到來自世界各地的禮物。 Max Hui So he's popular for getting gifts? 所以，牠因為收到禮物而受歡迎？ Estella Webber Well, no, it's not just getting the gifts. He's famous for opening the gifts. His viewers love to watch Mr Suess open the gifts that people send him. He got a cat-sized car last week. Did you see that one? 不是，重點不只是收到禮物，而是拆禮物。觀眾很喜歡看 Mr Suess 拆開大家寄給牠的禮物。牠上星期收到一輛適合貓大小的小汽車。你看過那段影片嗎？ Max Hui No, I think I missed it. 沒有，我想我錯過了。 Monica That's fascinating, Estella. But how do you train Mr Suess to do things for these videos? Aren't cats difficult to train? 很有趣，Estella。不過，你怎樣訓練 Mr Suess 拍這些影片？貓不是很難訓練嗎？ Estella Webber There are two main methods I use to train my cat. The first method is to place food rewards at the place where I want him to go. When Mr Suess goes to that certain spot, I give him a little food treat. 我主要用兩種方法訓練牠。第一種，是在我想牠走到的地方放食物獎勵。Mr Suess 到達那個指定位置時，我就給牠一點小食。 Monica Interesting. So what's the other method? 有意思。那另一種方法呢？ Estella Webber I repeat the action I want Mr Suess to perform. But here's the important part. I keep each session short. 我會重複想讓 Mr Suess 做的動作。不過，重點是每次訓練的時間都要短。 Monica Just to check that our viewers got that. You repeat the action you want him to do, but only for a short period each time. Why only a short period? 確認一下，讓觀眾聽清楚：你會重複想讓牠做的動作，但每次只維持短時間。為什麼每次只能練一會兒？ Estella Webber Cats have a very short attention span. If you try to get them to repeat an action for too long, the cat will lose interest. 貓能維持專注的時間很短。如果要牠重複一個動作太久，牠就會失去興趣。 Monica Now, Max, you've been studying this internet cat influencer phenomenon, and you've discovered that cat videos are much more popular than dog videos on YouTube. Why is that? Max，你一直研究貓網紅這個現象，而且發現 YouTube 上的貓影片比狗影片受歡迎得多。這是為什麼？ Max Hui Well, our research has shown that people prefer watching cat videos for two reasons. The first is that cats have lives that are more mysterious than dogs. 我們的研究顯示，人們偏愛貓影片有兩個原因。第一，貓的生活比狗更神秘。 Estella Webber That's so true. Mr Suess's life is a complete mystery to me. When I'm out of the flat, he gets up to all kinds of things. I'm so curious about what he does that I have cameras all over the house to record what he's doing when I'm not there. But even then he disappears. He's a real man of mystery. 太對了。Mr Suess 的生活對我來說完全是個謎。我不在家時，牠會做各種各樣的事。我太好奇了，所以在家中各處放了攝影機，記錄我不在時牠在做什麼。但即使這樣，牠還是會消失不見。牠真是個神秘的傢伙。 Max Hui And the second is that cat behaviour is less predictable than dog behaviour. What cats do is more surprising because of this. 第二，貓的行為比狗更難預測，因此牠們做的事更令人意外。 Estella Webber Oh gosh, yes. Dogs are so boringly predictable. I'm never surprised by what a dog does. 天啊，沒錯。狗的行為太容易預測，簡直有點無聊。狗做什麼，我都不會感到驚訝。 Monica Now, Max, you have expressed concern about owners like Estella here who use their cats for monetary gain on the internet. Max，你曾對像 Estella 這樣，利用自己的貓在網上賺錢的主人表示擔憂。 Max Hui Yes, I'm not saying that what Estella is doing does not have benefits for cats. For instance, our research has shown internet cat influencers like Mr Suess create positive feelings in their viewers. 是的。不過，我並不是說 Estella 所做的事對貓毫無好處。例如，我們的研究發現，像 Mr Suess 這類貓網紅能讓觀眾產生正面感受。 Estella Webber Mr Suess makes all his viewers feel positive. He's a very positive cat. Did your research also show that internet cats encourage people to adopt stray cats? Mr Suess 令所有觀眾都充滿正面情緒，牠是隻很積極的貓。你們的研究有沒有也發現，網絡上的貓會鼓勵人們領養流浪貓？ Max Hui Yes, our research did show that adoption of stray cats is linked to internet cat influencers. This is definitely a good thing for stray cats. But we do have concerns. 有，研究的確發現，流浪貓的領養與貓網紅有關聯。這對流浪貓肯定是好事。不過，我們確實有一些擔憂。 Monica Such as? 例如呢？ Max Hui Our main concern is with cat owners who abandon their cats once their cat stops being popular or making money. 我們最擔心的是，有些主人會在自己的貓不再受歡迎或不再賺錢時，便把牠們遺棄。 Estella Webber Oh, that's awful. I would never abandon Mr Suess. Even if he became unpopular, I would always keep him. 那太糟糕了。我絕不會遺棄 Mr Suess。即使牠不再受歡迎，我也一定會繼續照顧牠。 Monica I'm trying to imagine what might make a cat unpopular. Maybe some offensive tweet about birds? 我正在想，有什麼事會令一隻貓不再受歡迎呢？可能是發了一則冒犯雀鳥的推文吧？ Exam Narrator That's the end of task three. 任務三完結。 貓網紅 Mr Suess Monica 正在主持一場討論，主角是已成為知名網紅的貓 Mr Suess。與她一起參與討論的有貓主人 Estella Webber，以及香港貓咪收容所主席 Max Hui。請聆聽對話，並在下方筆記表記下資料。你不需要用完整句子作答。 Mr Suess（貓的名字） Mr Suess 的基本資料 擁有 名追蹤者。 根據 ，牠比 更有影響力。 Mr Suess 因哪些事情聞名？ Estella 訓練貓的方法 把食物獎勵放在她 的地方。 重複動作，但 ，因為 。 YouTube 上貓影片比狗影片受歡迎的原因 貓網紅帶來的好處 對貓網紅現象的擔憂

entries.title: Emojis as the new language of the Internet
entries.text: Candice and Monica have made a short documentary about the development of emojis as the new language of the Internet. Listen to the conversation and answer the questions below. You do not need to answer in complete sentences. History and background of emojis Vladimir Nabokov and Shigetaka Kurita Vladimir Nabokov · Shigetaka Kurita What did Vladimir Nabokov do in the 1950s which is similar to how we use emojis now? What is Shigetaka Kurita's contribution to the development of emojis? What is the current definition of an emoji? What is currently not considered an emoji? Interesting facts about a popular emoji Face blowing a kiss emoji What's the difference in how teenagers and married couples use this emoji? Teenagers: Married couples: Background on The World Committee for Emojis What are the two main functions of the committee? Main Function I: Main Function II: Concerns about The World Committee for Emojis Committee is made up of middle-aged white men Exam Narrator Task four. Candice and Monica have made a short documentary about the development of emojis as the new language of the internet. 任務四。Candice 和 Monica 製作了一齣短紀錄片，介紹表情符號如何發展成互聯網的新語言。 Exam Narrator Listen to the conversation and answer the questions below. Please note that you do not need to answer in complete sentences. You now have 30 seconds to study the task. At the end of the task, you will have three minutes to tidy up your answers. 請聆聽對話，並回答下列問題。請注意，你不需要用完整句子作答。你現在有三十秒時間閱讀題目。本任務結束後，你將有三分鐘時間整理答案。 Candice and Monica The emoji. Where do they come from? What fun facts can we learn about them? Do they have a dark side? Let's ask an expert. Hi there. 表情符號：它們從哪裡來？有什麼有趣的冷知識？它們有沒有黑暗的一面？我們來請教專家。你好。 Dr Antoni Badura This is Dr. Antoni Badura, and I'm a professor of computer science at the University of Hong Kong and also a current member of the World Committee for Emojis. Let's begin with a bit of history. The idea of using a picture of a face to show emotions goes back a long way. But when do we find things like emojis inserted into writing? The first person to do this might be the famous Russian novelist Vladimir Nabokov. 我是 Antoni Badura 博士，任教於香港大學電腦科學系，目前也是世界表情符號委員會成員。先談一點歷史吧。用臉部圖像表達情緒的概念由來已久。不過，人們是何時開始把類似表情符號的東西放進文字裡的呢？最早這樣做的人，可能是著名俄羅斯小說家 Vladimir Nabokov。 Dr Antoni Badura Back in the 1950s, Nabokov used brackets in his letters and correspondences to indicate to the reader that he was happy. I don't think anyone had used brackets to show happiness in everyday writing before then. But when we think of emojis as we use them today in online texting, there is one person who has arguably made the biggest contribution to the development of emojis, and that is Shigetaka Kurita. Back in the 90s, he was a designer for a mobile phone company, 早在 1950 年代，Nabokov 就在書信中使用括號，向讀者表示自己很開心。我想在那之前，還沒有人在日常文字中用括號表達快樂。不過，談到如今網上文字訊息中的表情符號，有一個人可說對它們的發展作出了最大的貢獻，那就是栗田穰崇（Shigetaka Kurita）。1990 年代，他在一家流動電話公司任職設計師， Dr Antoni Badura and while working there, he created the first set of emojis. Now, while other people claim to have used one or two emojis here or there, Kurita went much further and created a whole collection of emojis for use on mobile phones. This to me is the true beginning of emojis as we use them today. Presently, there is some debate about what is and what is not an emoji. Let me provide the latest definition that we experts in the industry subscribe to. 並在那裡工作期間創作了第一套表情符號。雖然其他人聲稱曾零星使用過一兩個表情符號，但 Kurita 做得更進一步：他創作了整套供流動電話使用的表情符號。在我看來，這才是今天這類表情符號真正的起點。目前，什麼算、什麼不算表情符號，仍有一些爭議。讓我介紹一下我們業內專家認同的最新定義。 Dr Antoni Badura An emoji is a picture that is used in texting to convey an emotion or an idea. So, when we say picture, we would mean something that is drawn, in which case a photograph cannot be an emoji. I'm not saying that this won't change in the future, but currently an emoji must be a drawn picture and not a photo. It is hard to understate how influential emojis are in our lives these days. 表情符號是一種用於文字訊息、傳達情緒或想法的圖像。我們所說的圖像，是指畫出來的東西；按這個定義，相片便不算表情符號。我不是說這個定義將來不會改變，但目前表情符號必須是繪製的圖像，而不是相片。如今，表情符號對我們生活的影響實在不容小覷。 Dr Antoni Badura Let's have a look at the most popular emoji in use around the world. I'm sure you've all used the emoji called face blowing a kiss. Well, here's a fun fact about this emoji. There are two groups of people who most use this emoji. One is teenagers who are flirting, and let's face it, emojis are a great way to flirt. And the other, somewhat surprisingly, is married couples. Apparently, married couples use this emoji not to flirt, but instead to show affection. 我們看看全球最常用的表情符號。我想大家都用過那個叫「飛吻臉」的圖案。它有一個有趣的現象：最常用它的是兩類人。一類是正在調情的青少年。說真的，表情符號是很好的調情工具。另一類可能有點令人意外，就是已婚伴侶。據說，已婚伴侶使用它並不是為了調情，而是表達愛意。 Dr Antoni Badura Now, as I said in my introduction, I'm a member of the World Committee for Emojis. So, what is this committee about? Well, it serves two functions. The first is to decide which emojis will be created. The emojis you find on your smartphones are not random or created by anyone who wants to make emojis. The committee decided which ones you should have. The second function of the committee is to standardise the codes for all emojis so that communication technologies will understand which emoji is being sent. 正如自我介紹時所說，我是世界表情符號委員會的成員。這個委員會做什麼呢？它有兩項職能。第一，是決定製作哪些表情符號。智能手機上的表情符號不是隨意出現的，也不是任何想做的人都能加入；是委員會決定哪些符號可供使用。第二，是統一所有表情符號的代碼，讓不同通訊技術辨認正在傳送的是哪一個符號。 Dr Antoni Badura Think about it. If the codes were not standardised, and each communication technology used a different code, then people with Apple iPhones could not send emojis to people with Samsung Galaxies. Here is a good place to talk about the darker side of emojis. Alas, it is not all smiles and laughter in the land of our cartoon friends. Even though I am a member, this still does not mean I agree with everything the committee does. 試想，如果代碼沒有統一，每種通訊技術各用不同代碼，那麼使用 Apple iPhone 的人就無法把表情符號傳給使用 Samsung Galaxy 的人。說到這裡，正好談談表情符號較陰暗的一面。唉，這個卡通朋友的世界並非只有歡笑。雖然我是委員會成員，也不代表我同意它所做的一切。 Dr Antoni Badura The first issue of concern is that the committee has too much control. That is one of the most common concerns people express. And as a result of the committee's control, we effectively have a limit on how people express themselves emotionally. Keep in mind that many emojis are a stand-in for the emotions we convey through body language and facial expressions when texting. And we should not limit this range of emotional expression. 第一個令人擔憂的問題，是委員會控制權過大。這是人們最常提出的擔憂之一。由於委員會的控制，我們表達情緒的方式實際上受到限制。要記住，在文字訊息中，很多表情符號代替了原本透過肢體語言和面部表情傳達的情緒。我們不應限制這些情緒表達的範圍。 Dr Antoni Badura This feeds into my second concern, which is that they, the committee, I mean, are all middle aged and white. Despite its title, the World Committee for Emojis is not actually representative of the many cultures and communities that use the internet. The committee, no matter how well intentioned, does not represent the vast diversity of people from different cultures and communities around the world. In my view, we cannot continue to have a committee that comprises entirely 這也牽涉到我的第二個擔憂：他們——我是指委員會成員——全是中年白人。儘管名為「世界表情符號委員會」，它實際上未能代表使用互聯網的眾多文化和社群。無論出發點多好，委員會都不能代表世界各地不同文化和社群的多元人士。在我看來，我們不能繼續讓委員會完全由 Dr Antoni Badura of a bunch of middle-aged male Western computer engineers. My third concern is that the work of the committee is not made public enough. It needs to open its doors and let the public see what it is doing. If it does not make its work more public, then this will lead to suspicion. We do not want people to become suspicious of the committee because they lack the opportunity to look at its work or think that the committee is somehow secretive 一群中年西方男性電腦工程師組成。我的第三個擔憂，是委員會的工作不夠公開。它需要敞開大門，讓公眾了解自己在做什麼。如果不提高工作的公開程度，就會引起猜疑。我們不希望人們因為沒有機會了解委員會的工作，便對它產生懷疑，或認為它行事隱秘， Dr Antoni Badura and beyond scrutiny. 而且不受審視和監察。 Dr Antoni Badura Well, that's it from me. Hope you found my guide to the world of emojis an interesting one. 我的介紹就到這裡。希望大家覺得這趟表情符號世界導覽有趣。 表情符號：互聯網的新語言 Candice 和 Monica 製作了一齣短紀錄片，介紹表情符號如何發展成互聯網的新語言。請聆聽對話，並回答下列問題。你不需要用完整句子作答。 表情符號的歷史與背景 Vladimir Nabokov（弗拉基米爾・納博科夫）與 Shigetaka Kurita（栗田穰崇） Vladimir Nabokov 在 1950 年代做了什麼，與我們今天使用表情符號的方式相似？ Shigetaka Kurita 對表情符號的發展有什麼貢獻？ 目前表情符號的定義是什麼？ 目前有什麼不被視為表情符號？ 一個熱門表情符號的有趣資訊 「飛吻臉」表情符號 青少年和已婚伴侶使用這個表情符號的方式有什麼不同？ 青少年： 已婚伴侶： 世界表情符號委員會的背景 委員會的兩項主要職能是什麼？ 主要職能一： 主要職能二： 對世界表情符號委員會的擔憂 表格欄目：擔憂／後果。 擔憂： 後果： 擔憂：委員會由中年白人男性組成。 後果： 擔憂： 後果：
